people.name: Evald Johannes Gaardsted-Jørgensen
people.note: Døbt 8. okt. 1922 i Kolind Kirke af pastor J.P. Jensen. Faddere: enken Rasmine Kristine Gaardsted (farmor), fattiggårdsbestyrer Martin Marinus Gaardsted, Bregnet, og ungkarl Axel Vilhelm Alfred Gaardsted (morbrødre). Navneforandring til Gaardsted-Jørgensen ved navnebevis 1983/1985 (randnote). Romaner bl.a. 'De kom til en by' (1999, om flytningen til Hadsten 1932), 'Skriv hjem, Niels' og 'Jos og hans verden'; 'Leck Fischer. Signalement af en digter' (1973). Hans personarkiv med en egen slægtstavle ligger i Hadsten Lokalarkiv (A37).

people.name: Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen
people.note: Det borgerlige fødselsregister for Egernsund (1932 nr. 4, anmeldt 16. jan. 1932) siger, at Else Gedde Frederiksen, f. Jensen, fødte ham 12. jan. 1932 kl. 5.30. En randnote af 11. juli 1932 siger, at landarbejder Wilhelm Krogh fra Snogbæk er den biologiske far. Det bygger på hans faderskabserklæring af 5. april 1932 og en retsafgørelse af 10. juni 1932. Stedfaren Peter Frederiksen gav drengen sit efternavn. Det stemmer med familiens fortælling om, at Lorenz først som voksen fandt ud af, at Peter ikke var hans far. Familiens viden er, at den biologiske far var gårdmandssønnen Sophus Petersen fra Påkjær i Nybøl, at landarbejder Wilhelm Krogh tog skylden, og at Peter Frederiksen blev betalt for at gifte sig med Else. Faderskabet vises derfor som to særskilte, omstridte oplysninger og ikke som en fastslået biologisk forælder. Ifølge dåbsindførslen i Broager Vestre distrikt (1933 nr. 1) var fadderne stedfaren selv, arbejdsmand Lorenz Frederiksen og hustru Catharina, Egernsund, samt gårdejer Jens Jensens hustru fra Dalsgaard. Lorenz er begravet sammen med hustruen Gerda på Sankt Jørgens Kirkegård i Svendborg. Familiens opgørelse skriver født 10. jan. 1932 (fødselsregistret: 12. jan.). Konfirmeret palmesøndag 1946. Gift 25. nov. 1954 i Magleby Kirke med Gerda Larsen. Familien fortæller: Indtil han var 40, vidste han ikke andet, end at Peter Frederiksen var hans far. Han fik så at vide, at Peter havde giftet sig med Else et par måneder før fødslen, men at det ikke var ham, der var faren. Det blev der ikke talt om. Lorenz fandt senere ud af, at faren var gårdejer Sofus Petersen fra Paakjær i Nybøl.

people.name: Gerda Frederiksen (f. Larsen)
people.note: Født 17. aug. 1935 i Nordenbro, Magleby sogn på Sydlangeland, og hjemmedøbt dagen efter. Fremstillet i Magleby Kirke 3. nov. 1935. Forældre: tømrer Laurits Edvard Larsen og Karen Margrethe Holgersen. Faddere: gårdmand Johannes Nielsen og hustru, Haugbølle, samt bødker Aksel Holgersen, Kædeby (hendes morfar). Gennem sin mormor Kristine er hun oldebarn af Marius Christensen, 'Kongen af Langø', som købte øen Langø i Lindelse Nor i 1894 og i 1911 byggede dæmningen til Langeland. Begravet på Sankt Jørgens Kirkegård i Svendborg sammen med sin mand Lorenz. Hjemmedøbt 18. aug. 1935 i Nordenbro, konfirmeret 16. april 1950, gift 25. nov. 1954 i Magleby Kirke (familiens anetavle). MyHeritage-træet giver dødsåret 2019.

people.name: Marius Michelsen Christensen
occ: Landbruger og ejer af øen Langø (1894–)
Arbejdsmand ved Rudkøbing havn og Frihavnen i København
people.note: 'Kongen af Langø'. Han købte øen Langø i Lindelse Nor i 1894 sammen med hustruen Ane Marie, og i 1911 byggede han med håndkraft og hjælp fra sønner og svigersøn den 334 m lange dæmning, som gjorde øen landfast. Ifølge familien gik Langø senere i arv til efterkommere med navnet Pedersen. Flere af familiens slægtninge fra Sydlangeland udvandrede til Amerika. Barnebarnet Lisbeth Skov, født Christensen, fortæller i 'En Langø-piges erindringer', at øen før 1894 havde hørt under Hjortholm gods og siden tre gårde i Haugbølle, som brugte den til græsning: kreaturerne blev svømmet over om foråret og hjem om efteråret. En skomager havde købt øen og bygget et simpelt hus, men den kom på tvangsauktion, hvorefter Marius og Ane Marie købte den. Fra barnebarnet Lisbeth Skovs erindringer: Marius var ved landbruget og arbejdsmand, var med til at bygge Rudkøbing havn og hjalp derefter med at grave Frihavnen i København ud (han fandt en kanonkugle i havnen, som stadig er på Langø). Tilbage i Rudkøbing købte parret et lille husmandssted på Spodsbjergvej, og Marius arbejdede på Langelands Korn for 2 kr. om dagen. Ejeren af Baygården, formand for Langelands Bank, der havde overtaget Langø ved tvangsauktion, overtalte dem til at købe øen for 4.000 kr. med 1.600 kr. i udbetaling. I 1894 flyttede familien derud med fire børn. Fra 11. jan. 1911 byggede Marius og sønnerne en dæmning til Kædeby Haver, til sidst 334 meter lang og 6–8 meter bred; myndighederne mente ikke, han ville nå det i sin, sine børns eller børnebørns tid.

people.name: Lars Thomsen
people.note: Født i Magleby. Gårdfæster i Magleby, Langeland. Gift ca. 1816 med Anne Cathrine Jensdatter fra Fangel på Fyn; børn: Thomas (1817), Karen (1818), Jens (1820), Laurine (1823), Johanne Marie (1825), Peder Christian (1830) og Lars (1832). Sandsynligvis den Lars Thomasen, der 1801 tjente i Magleby, søn af husmand Thomas Jensen (FT 1787). MyHeritage-træet gør Lars Larsens far til en Lars Larsen f. 1771 i Rutsker, død 1854 i Allinge, og fører derfra slægten 8 led tilbage på Bornholm. Det er en fejlagtig automatisk kobling: folketællingerne 1834–50 viser Lars Larsen hjemme hos sin far, gårdmand Lars Thomsen i Magleby, og sønnesønnen hedder Lars Thomsen Larsen. Bornholm-grenen er derfor ikke taget med.

people.name: Wilhelm Krogh
people.rel: tog skylden: anerkendte faderskabet til Lorenz i 1932
people.note: Ifølge familien tog han skylden for gårdmandssønnen Sophus Petersen fra Påkjær. I det borgerlige register står han som Lorenz' far. Født 9. okt. 1908 i 'Tastrup' (eller 'Vastrup'; skriften er svær at læse), Landkreis Flensburg, dengang i Tyskland. Faderskabet står i randnoten i Egernsund-registret: han anerkendte faderskabet 5. april 1932, og retten afgjorde sagen 10. juni 1932. Hans forældre og hans videre liv er endnu ikke fundet. De står i tyske registre (Flensburg). Der boede en anden Krogh-familie i Nybøl: arbejder Detlef Krogh (f. 8. maj 1905), gift 1929 i Broager med Cecilie Marie f. Hansen, fik døtre i Nybøl 1936 og 1940. I 1921 boede Detlef Krogh (f. 1849) og Botilde (f. 1850) i Nybøl. De kan være Wilhelms bror og bedsteforældre, men det er ikke bekræftet.
src: AO:Egernsund standsregister, fødte 1928–33, 1932 nr. 4, randnote 11.7.1932 (bsid 37658, billede 125)
AO:Nybøl kirkebog 1931–58, fødte piger 1936 og 1940 (Detlef Krogh)

people.name: Sophus (Sofus) Petersen
people.note: Født 28. juni 1903 og døbt 24. juli 1903 i Nybøl Kirke (kirkebogen 1903 nr. 12) som søn af gårdmand ('Hufner') Peter Petersen og hustru Anna Cathrine Marie f. Petersen i Nybøl. Faddere: gæstgiver Johannes Hansen i Hostrup, tjenestekarl Jürgen Jacobsen i Nybøl og ugift Marie Iversen i Schottsbüllfeld. Fødselsdatoen passer præcist med gravstenen på Nybøl Kirkegård. Familien har fået at vide, at Lorenz' far hed Sophus og var fra Påkjær gård i Nybøl, og at han som gårdmandssøn ikke kunne vedstå faderskabet. I stedet tog landarbejder Wilhelm Krogh skylden: han anerkendte faderskabet i 1932, og retten stadfæstede det, så det er Krogh, der står i standsregistret. Påkjær ligger i Nybøl sogn tæt ved Snogbæk, hvor Krogh var karl i 1932. Sophus døde kun 42 år gammel. Han og hustruen Christine fik tre døtre: Gerda og to andre, hvoraf den ene flyttede til Norge. De er Lorenz' halvsøstre. En DNA-test kan bekræfte slægtskabet. Familiens anetavle: gårdejer, død af lungekræft 24. aug. 1945 på Paakjær i Nybøl. Familiens opgørelse: 'I dennes ægteskab var 4 døtre, der var Lorenz's halvsøstre.'
src: Gravsten på Nybøl Kirkegård (foto fra familien): 'Minde over en elsket Mand og Fader Sofus Petersen, Paakjær, * 28. Juni 1903 † 24. Aug. 1945'

people.name: Else Gedde Jensen
people.note: Født 31. aug. 1912 i Ferup, Lejrskov sogn, og døbt 20. okt. 1912 i Lejrskov Kirke. Faddere: frøken Mathilde Gedde, København (moster/grandtante på Gedde-siden), Kirstine Jensen og købmand Jørgen Jensen, Haderslev. Her kommer navnet Gedde fra: Else fik det som mellemnavn efter sin mor, Paula Gedde. I januar 1932 var hun gift med arbejdsmand Peter Frederiksen i Egernsund. Gift 15. nov. 1931 i Egernsund med Peter Frederiksen. Død 30. jan. 1975 på Sønderborg Sygehus (familiens opgørelse og anetavle).

people.name: Ove Frederik Christopher Gedde
people.note: Hjemmedøbt i Fredensborg, indført i kirkebogen 24. juli 1808 som søn af 'Hr. Capitaine ved Kronens Regiment Hr. Ove Samuel Giedde og Frue Frederikke Lovise Birthe født Kleist'. Faddere: oberstløjtnantinde Recke, jomfru Gradman fra Helsingør, kaptajn Giedde fra Helsingør og løjtnanterne Tønnesen og Bøgtrup. Han voksede op i Herlufmagle Præstegård hos sin moster Christine Sophie von Kleist og hendes mand, sognepræst dr.theol. Edvard Snedorph Hammer. Gift 16. okt. 1840 i Helligånds Kirke, København, med Charlotte Frederikke Christine Møller. I 1840–50 bestyrede han Viborggaard i Herlufmagle for mosteren, der var enke og ejede gården. Hendes bror, pensionist Ludvig Adam Kleist, boede der også. Begge var født i Assens.

people.name: Ove Samuel Gedde
occ: Officer: sekondløjtnant, kaptajn (1808), oberstløjtnant og bataljonschef ved Kronens Regiment
people.note: Gift 24. juni 1806 med Frederikke Louise Dorthea von Kleist. Kaldes 'von Gedde' i folketællingen 1834, hvor familien bor i Helsingør med datteren Henriette (f. 1819). Han er familiens bedste bud på 'kaptajnen' i fortællingen om navnet Gedde: Else Gedde Jensens tipoldefar og kaptajn i 1808. Der er dog intet i kilderne om, at han var i Trankebar.

people.name: Frederikke Louise Dorthea von Kleist
people.note: Kirkebogen 1808 kalder hende 'Frederikke Lovise Birthe født Kleist'. Datter af kammerherre Christian Frederik von Kleist. Hendes søster Christine Sophie var gift med pastor Hammer i Herlufmagle, og søsteren Juliane med den norske generalmajor Nicolai Wilhelm Gedde, sandsynligvis Ove Samuels bror.

people.name: Hans Christopher Gedde
people.note: Stamfar til den norske Gedde-slægt. Hans søn Nicolai Wilhelm Gedde (1779–1833) giftede sig med Frederikke Louises søster. Geni angiver ham som far til Ove Samuel, men det er ikke bekræftet i en primærkilde.

people.name: Øllegaard Sophie Fischer
people.note: Kaldes andre steder 'Frederikke Christiane Fischer'.

people.name: Samuel Christoph Gedde
people.note: Far til ti børn, bl.a. Hans Christopher (f. 1738). Ifølge Store norske leksikon har den borgerlige Gedde-slægt sandsynligvis ingen forbindelse til den uddøde adelsslægt Gjedde, som Trankebars grundlægger, admiral Ove Gjedde, tilhørte.

people.name: Christian Frederik von Kleist
people.note: Gift 3. dec. 1770 med Anna Margrethe Schubart. Fire sønner og fire døtre, bl.a. generalmajor Carl Gottlieb von Kleist.

people.name: Christian Adam von Kleist
occ: Amtmand i Rendsborg (1740) og landråd i Holsten
people.note: Døbt i Vor Frelsers Kirke på Christianshavn. Ridder af Dannebrog 1759. Død i Bredsted og begravet i Slesvig Domkirke.

people.name: Sophie Rosenkrantz
people.note: Dame de l'Union parfaite 1752. Begravet i Slesvig Domkirke.

people.name: Cartz Ulrik von Kleist
people.note: Fra Muttrin-linjen af den pommerske adelsslægt von Kleist. Han var i brandenborgsk tjeneste 1692–94 og i dansk tjeneste fra 1701. Han blev såret og taget til fange ved Helsingborg i 1710 og ved Gadebusch i 1712. Han døde i Rendsborg og blev begravet 17. nov. 1722. Parret fik 10 børn.

people.name: Barbara Juliane von Kleist
people.note: Boede endnu i 1730 på godset Drenow i Pommern.

people.name: Pribislaff von Kleist
occ: Godsejer: Muttrin, Borntin, Döbel og Drenow (Pommern)

people.name: Christian Casimir von Kleist
occ: Kaptajn og chef for grenaderkompagniet ved Fynske Infanteriregiment (1685)
people.note: Arvede en del af Gross Tychow i Pommern. Han deltog i felttoget i hertugdømmerne i 1700 og døde i Oldenborg.

people.name: Anna von Fürst
people.note: Fra Schlesien.

people.name: Christian von Kleist
people.note: Stamfar til den gren af slægten, der 'i henimod halvandet hundrede år blomstrede i Danmark'.

people.name: Hedvig Maria von Kleist
people.note: Hans første hustru. Hun bragte en del af Gross Tychow med ind i ægteskabet.

people.name: Christina von Woyten
people.note: Ingen fødsels- eller dødsdato er oplyst i de anvendte slægtshistoriske kilder. VKA, Dubberow 2025, s. 143 (II.55), identificerer hende som enke efter Otto von Below og hustru til Georg von Kleist på Groß-Tychow; samme værk omtaler på s. 36 (II.44) en Christina Woyten fra Versin som første hustru til en anden Georg von Kleist, uden børn. Om det er samme kvinde i to på hinanden følgende ægteskaber, eller to navnesøstre, er ikke afgjort. Datoer må ikke udledes af hendes fars dødsgrænse. Identitetsspørgsmålet undersøges fortsat.

people.name: Benedictus (Benedict) von Woyten
people.note: Died after 6 December 1584. Father of Christina von Woyten.

people.name: Elisabeth von Stojentin
people.note: Of Giesebitz; mother of Christina von Woyten.

people.name: Otto von Below of Pustamin
people.note: Christina von Woyten’s first husband; she was his widow when she married Georg von Kleist.

people.name: Conradus Clest
people.note: Nævnt i 1248 (Urk. 26). Urk. 27 (17. juni 1249) kalder Bertoldus og Conradus Clest brødre; Urk. 32a (1254) og Urk. 48 (7. april 1269) støtter samme søskendepar. Der er ikke påvist forbindelse til vidnegruppen fra 1289 eller til den senere Muttrin-linje.

people.name: Bertoldus (Bartoldus) Clest
people.note: Urk. 27 (17. juni 1249) kalder Bertoldus og Conradus Clest brødre. Urk. 32a (1254) og Urk. 48 (7. april 1269) omtaler samme Bertoldus som Conradus' bror. Ingen dokumenteret forbindelse til den senere Muttrin-linje.

people.name: Prissebur (vidne 1289)
people.note: Urk. 75 (1289) nævner Prissebur og Clest blandt Pribislaus af Daber/Belgard's ministeriales. Den omstridte formulering 'prissebur, clest fratres' gør det usikkert, om Prissebur og Clest var brødre, eller om 'fratres' sigter til Clest-brødrene. Identiteten er ikke koblet til Prissebur Klest af Muttrin i 1364.

people.name: Nycolaus Klest
people.note: Navngivet som vidne i Urk. 3888, 13. november 1325, ved en grænsesag med Dargun kloster. Dokumentet angiver ikke bopæl, status, forældre eller forbindelse til andre Clest/Klest-navne.

people.name: Prissebur Klest af Muttrin
people.note: Urk. 83, 22. juni 1364, betegner ham som 'Prissebur Klest von Muttrin' og omtaler hans andel af 25 huder ved Glyne/Glienke. Udgaven bygger på et transsumpt fra 1589 og senere kopier, ikke på det originale 1364-pergament. Dokumentet fastslår ikke hans forældre eller de mellemliggende led frem til den senere Muttrin-slægt.

people.name: Emil Ludvig Edvard Gedde
people.note: Udvandrede i 1922 til Argentina med hustruen Olivia (Johanne Marie Olivia f. Eddelsen) og to børn, og døde der i 1951. Sønnen Ejler blev i Argentina og døde omkring 1990 uden kendte børn. Datteren Inge Regitze (f. 1911, død ca. 1950) vendte tilbage til Danmark i 1930'erne og blev gift med Arne Meyer; ingen børn. Udvandrerarkivet har to billeder fra den danske koloni i Eldorado, Argentina: 'De ældste medlemmer af den danske koloni' (1920–30), hvor 'Gedde, landbrugskandidat, over 50 år' sidder forrest, og en konfirmationsfest 27. okt. 1935 med 'fru Gedde' og 'hr Gedde'.

people.name: Christen (Kresten) Henriksen Jørgensen
people.rel: Lars Thomsen Larsens uægte søn (Laurits Edvards halvbror)
people.note: Født 3. nov. 1877 i Søndenbro, Magleby sogn, med Lars Thomsen Larsen som far og Marthe Jørgensen som mor. Lars var 18 år. Kresten boede i 1880 og 1890 hos Jørgen Christensen og Karen Andersen i Magleby, som 'andet' (plejebarn). Konfirmationen 1893 og vielsen 1907 nævner begge Lars Thomsen Larsen som far. Konfirmationsindekset har fejlagtigt fødselsdatoen 23. feb. 1879. Dødsår og sted er ikke fundet. To mulige mødre: (A) Marthe Christine Jørgensen, født 25. jan. 1837 (Tryggelev), gift 1861 i Magleby med Thomas Rasmussen Jespersen (1841–1891) og mor til syv Jespersen-børn 1860–1876; hun lever endnu i 1921 hos datteren Ane. (B) Marthe Jørgensen, født 9. okt. 1852, datter af Jørgen Christensen (Stougaard) og Karen Andersen, død 27. aug. 1878. Dåben 1877 nævner kun 'Marthe Jørgensen' og ingen ægtemand. Krestens plejefamilie i 1880 og 1890 var netop Jørgen Christensen og Karen Andersen, hvilket peger på B. Men hans folketællingsfamilie havde også andre plejebørn, så det er ikke afgørende. En Google-søgning (MyHeritage) giver Marthe Jørgensen fra Søndenbro tre andre børn, Margrethe, Nielsine Marie og Otto August Jørgensen. De findes ikke i Magleby kirkebog under hendes navn, så det er uverificeret.
res: hos morforældrene Jørgen Christensen og Karen Andersen

claims.title: Wilhelm Kroghs registrerede faderskab
claims.claim: Egernsund standsregisters randnote angiver Wilhelm Krogh som far efter en faderskabserklæring 5. april 1932 og en retsafgørelse 10. juni 1932. Det dokumenterer registreringen og sagsforløbet, men ikke i sig selv biologisk faderskab.
claims.evidence: Dossieret identificerer Egernsund standsregister, fødte 1928–33, 1932 nr. 4 (bsid 37658, billede 125), samt Broager Vestre kirkebog 1933 nr. 1. Kildereferencerne er registreret; selve sagsakterne er ikke fuldt gennemgået i denne offentlige oversigt.
claims.missing: Den fulde faderskabssag, ordlyden af erklæringen og retsafgørelsen samt eventuelle samtidige breve eller vidneudsagn. Biologisk slægtskab kræver særskilt evidens.
claims.next: Find og gennemgå den originale faderskabssag og sammenhold den med øvrige samtidige kilder.

claims.title: Sophus Petersen som biologisk far
claims.claim: Familien har fortalt, at gårdmandssønnen Sophus Petersen fra Påkjær i Nybøl var Lorenz' biologiske far, mens Wilhelm Krogh påtog sig faderskabet. Det er en vigtig familieoplysning, men den er i konflikt med den officielle registrering.
claims.evidence: Familiedokumentet, den håndskrevne anetavle og familiens mundtlige overlevering identificerer Sophus. Sophus' dåb og gravsten underbygger hans identitet og livsforløb, ikke faderskabet til Lorenz.
claims.missing: Uafhængig dokumentation for forbindelsen mellem Sophus og Lorenz, fx samtidige breve, vidneudsagn eller relevant DNA-sammenligning med dokumenteret slægt.
claims.next: Opsøg efterladte familiepapirer og vurder muligheden for DNA-sammenligning med kendte efterkommere af Sophus.

claims.title: Liss' vielse i 1843: uoverensstemmelse om ægtefællens navn
claims.claim: Der er en uafklaret forskel mellem navnene Kjersten Frederiksdatter og Mette Pedersdatter i materialet om ægtefællen. Vielsen i Sønder Felding i 1843 er udpeget som den centrale kontrolkilde.

claims.missing: Den originale vielsesindførsel og sammenligning af alder, bopæl, forlovere og forældrenavne med de øvrige personer i husstanden.
claims.next: Find vielsesindførslen i Sønder Felding og registrér dens præcise ordlyd og billedhenvisning.

claims.title: Dåb i Pårup Melgaard, 1812

claims.evidence: Sporet er noteret i den aktive Liss-dossier som en målrettet kirkebogskontrol, ikke som en fastslået identifikation.
claims.missing: Original dåbsindførsel samt match på forældre, alder og senere bopæl/vielse.
claims.next: Kontrollér kirkebogen og sammenhold alle navne- og stedvarianter.

claims.title: Vibygård og Syv: mulig identitetssammenhæng

claims.evidence: Den aktive Evald-dossier samler dette som et åbent identitetsspor. Der er endnu ikke fremlagt en sammenhængende kæde af originale dokumenter her.

research_notes.title: Bogensholm and Vosnæsgaard
research_notes.context: 2. Gaardsted / Vosnæsgaard / Rolsøgård
research_notes.text:
Claus Gaardsted is recorded as tenant at Vosnæsgaard and later owner of Bogensholm. The project notes a discrepancy in the purchase year: Trap Danmark references 1796, while another Trap entry gives 1797. A royal rescript of 6 August 1803 addresses Claus as owner of Bogensholm. He died in 1811; his widow sold the estate at auction for 31,000 rigsdaler.

Sources:
- [Trap Danmark — Vistoft parish](https://trap5.lex.dk/sogn/vistoft-sogn-mols-herred/)
- [Royal rescript, 6 August 1803](https://da.wikisource.org/wiki/Side:Kongelige_Rescripter,_Resolutioner_og_Collegialbreve_for_Danmark_og_Norge_udtogsvis_udgivne_i_chronologisk_Orden._VI._Deel._12._Bind_(1803%E2%80%931804).pdf/258)
- [Vosnæsgaard drawing, 1839](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sloev/tree/main/images/vosnaesgaard-1839-rawert.jpg) — contextual image, not proof of the earlier household.

claims.title: Kresten Henriksen Jørgensens dåb, 1877
claims.claim: Dåben i 1877 er et åbent spor til at afklare Krestens forældre og den korrekte placering i Langø-grenen.
claims.evidence: Den aktive Gerda-dossier udpeger dåbsindførslen som kontrolpunkt. Der er endnu ikke gengivet en verificeret transskription i denne oversigt.
claims.missing: Original kirkebogsindførsel, faddere og bopælsoplysninger samt sammenhold med senere vielse og folketællinger.
claims.next: Kontrollér dåbsbilledet og følg familien gennem senere kilder.

claims.title: Langø: skøde fra 1894 og vej/dæmning omkring 1911
claims.claim: Et skøde fra 1894 og myndighedsforhold omkring vej eller dæmning i 1911 kan belyse ejerskab og lokale forhold ved Langø.
claims.evidence: Begge spor er nævnt i den aktive Gerda-dossier som konkrete arkivopgaver. Det er endnu ikke fastslået, hvad dokumenterne præcist siger.
claims.missing: Originalt skøde samt kommunale, amtslige eller vejmyndighedsakter fra omkring 1911 med klar angivelse af ansvar, dato og berørte ejendomme.
claims.next: Identificér arkivskaber og journal-/tingbogsnummer, og gennemgå originalakterne.

claims.title: Rolsøgård-skiftet 1764: Tohde og stedbørnene
claims.claim: Et skifte fra 1764 efter Christen Christensen med tilnavnet muligvis “Tohde” kan belyse Claus Gaardsteds og Karen Christensdatters familieforhold. Dossierets læsning af en senere skiftehenvisning beskriver dem som stedbørn — ikke som hans biologiske børn.
claims.evidence: Evald-dossieret peger på Rolsøgård Gods, skifteprotokol G302, og skiftet i Dejret fra 1764. En senere 1787-henvisning bruger ifølge dossierets foreløbige læsning ordet “stedbørn”.
claims.missing: Originalen fra 1764 og den præcise ordlyd i Rolsøgård G302 nr. 11, 14. maj 1787, folio 39. Den biologiske forælder til Claus og Karen er ikke identificeret.
claims.next: Bestil og læs begge originale skifter; transskriber slægtskabsordene før nogen forældretilknytning ændres.

research_notes.title: 13. Clarification: Tohde was a stepfather, not an established biological father
research_notes.context: 13. Clarification: Tohde was a stepfather, not an established biological father
research_notes.text:
The evidence-audit compilation parses the G302 clause as describing Karen Christensdatter and Claus Gaardsted as **stepchildren** of Christen Christensen “Tohde?” (foged in Dejret; probate 1764). This is consistent with the word `stedbørn`. The 1787 index therefore does **not** identify the biological father of Claus or Karen. It supports the sibling relationship and points to Tohde's earlier probate, which may name the biological parent(s). The exact wording must still be checked on the original folio 39.

The old extension's proposed patch that creates Christen Christensen Tohde as biological father of Claus and Karen, renames Claus “Claus Christensen”, and adds a FAMC is not approved. Keep the current blank parent fields until the original 1764 probate and the original 1787 folio are read.

A separate research note raises **Mette Sørensdatter Helles** as an alternative identity in the Rosmus material. Do not merge the women or silently substitute one for the other. Compare the original marriage, baptism, census and probate records, including the exact surname/patronymic reading. The family tree's current Hallis link is the working hypothesis, not a final resolution of every name variant.

The canonical chain includes Rasmus Jensen Rousing (`p76`), his son Anders Rasmussen Rousing (`p38`) and granddaughter Rasmine Christine Andersen (`p19`). The proposed parent Jens Rasmussen (`p152`) is marked probable because Rasmus, age 20, appears in his 1801 household. The earlier Rasmus Jensen (`p304`) is only a possible father based on name pattern; this is not enough to establish parentage.

Next steps: inspect Fuglslev parish records, 1787/1801 censuses, probate and the relevant herred appointment records. Do not promote `p304` to a parent without direct evidence.

research_notes.title: 14. Rousing and Viby extra source details
research_notes.context: 14. Rousing and Viby extra source details
research_notes.text:
- The 1787 Fuglslev census lists a Rasmus Jensen, farmer, age 70 (approx. birth 1717/1718), which is consistent with but does not prove the possible `p304` identity. The 1801 household of Jens Rasmussen (`p152`) with a 20-year-old Rasmus is the actual basis for the probable `p152` → `p76` link.

- Hans Jensen (`a66`) and Margaretha Pedersdatter (`a67`) have no recorded parents. Search Viby pre-1814 baptisms for Hans around 1752 and Syv baptisms for Margaretha around 1797. The Vibygaard estate accounts may list Hans as a gardener.
- The 1820 Vibygaard probate and the 1822 Syv marriage are still the key identity pair. A probate transcription is a strong clue but not a substitute for the original 1822 marriage entry.

research_notes.context: 4. Pårup Melgaard / Assing / Sønder Felding — direct ancestral lead

Jens Peder Larsen (`a46`), born about 1812 in Assing, is a direct ancestor through Karen Jensen (`p23`), Hulda's mother. The current tree identifies his wife as **Kjersten Frederiksdatter** (`a47`), born 20 April 1822 in Sønder Felding, daughter of Frederik Jensen and Ane Thomasdatter. **Spouse discrepancy:** an uploaded expanded dossier says Jens Peder married Mette Pedersdatter in 1843. The existing tree and Horsbøl genealogy instead identify Kjersten Frederiksdatter, married 8 October 1843 in Sønder Felding. Horsbøl also lists their daughter Mette Marie, which may explain the dossier's mistaken Mette. The current working identification is Kjersten, but the original 1843 marriage entry must be inspected before treating the conflict as fully closed.

- [Horsbøl — Sønder Omme 1870 census](https://www.horsboel.dk/fkt/FKT_Sdr_Omme_1870.pdf)

The Assing births before 1814 are not indexed in the same way as later records. Search the original Assing register and adjacent parishes. Preserve the uncertain date as circa 1812 unless the original entry confirms it.

claims.title: Kresten Jørgensen: hvilken Marthe var hans mor?

claims.evidence: Dossieret nævner dåbsindekset LL:12-16292169 og folketællingerne 1880 og 1890, hvor Kresten skal være opvokset hos Jørgen Christensen og Karen Andersen. Det kan pege mod Marthe Jørgensen (født 1852), men er indirekte.

research_notes.title: 3. Kresten Henriksen Jørgensen — possible non-marital child
research_notes.context: 3. Kresten Henriksen Jørgensen — possible non-marital child
research_notes.text:
**Status: unresolved family-chart claim.**

The family chart reportedly records Kresten, born 3 November 1877, as an illegitimate son of Lars Thomsen Larsen (`p28`) who was raised by the mother's parents. The relevant handwritten field is partly obscured by an ink blot; the mother's name and exact parish record are not yet identified. A prior exact-name web search and check of the Strømming public K-name index found no match. This is only a negative index result, not evidence that Kresten or the baptism does not exist.

Tasks:
- Reinspect the original family chart and identify the mother and exact wording.
- Search 1877 birth/baptism registers in Magleby and neighbouring South Langeland parishes, including illegitimate-birth columns and marginal notes.
- Check maintenance/alimentation cases, acknowledgement records, confirmation registers and 1880/1890/1901 censuses.
- Establish whether “Henriksen Jørgensen” is a contemporary recorded name or a later name.
- Do not encode Lars Thomsen Larsen as father until the original entry or corroborating evidence supports it.

research_notes.title: 12. Kresten and the two possible mothers named Marthe Jørgensen
research_notes.context: 12. Kresten and the two possible mothers named Marthe Jørgensen
research_notes.text:
The family chart's lead is more specific than the earlier summary. It gives **Christen Henriksen Jørgensen** (`g_kresten`), born 3 November 1877 at Søndenbro, as a possible non-marital son of Lars Thomsen Larsen (`p28`), aged 18, and a woman recorded as Marthe Jørgensen (`g_marthe`). The mother's identity remains unresolved.

Two candidates are preserved:
- **Candidate A:** Marthe Christine Jørgensen, born 25 January 1837 at Tryggelev; married Thomas Rasmussen Jespersen in 1861; had seven children and was alive in 1921.
- **Candidate B:** Marthe Jørgensen, born 9 October 1852, daughter of Jørgen Christensen (Stougaard) and Karen Andersen; died 27 August 1878.

The extension leans toward candidate B because Kresten's foster parents in the 1880 and 1890 censuses were Jørgen Christensen and Karen Andersen, who were candidate B's parents. Candidate B's death in 1878 does not rule her out as Kresten's mother, but it means she could not have raised him after his birth. This is a hypothesis, not proof. A plausible age/household inference must not replace the original baptism.

**Decisive checks, in order:**
1. Read the full 1877 baptism entry cited as `LL:12-16292169`, not only the index. It reportedly names “Marthe Jørgensen” without a husband; inspect age, residence, employer (“tjener på”) and marginal notes.
2. Read candidate B's 27 August 1878 burial. If a surviving child is named, that is significant; absence of a child does not by itself disprove maternity.
3. Inspect the Magleby tilgangsliste for 1877 for the mother's residence and any child placement.
4. Search candidate A's 1921 census household for Kresten.
5. Test the MyHeritage claim that “Marthe Jørgensen fra Søndenbro” had three further children (Margrethe, Nielsine Marie and Otto August). These are not found in the Magleby register under her name in the existing notes; births after August 1878 cannot belong to candidate B.

Other open points:
- Kresten's death has not been found.
- Magleby church book 1916 reportedly names an unnamed child of Kresten and Marie Laurentine, born 15 January 1916 (`g_kbarn`). Read the full entry and identify whether the child was stillborn, unnamed at registration, or later named.
- The prior exact-name web search and Strømming K-name index returned no match; this is a scoped negative search, not proof of non-existence.

claims.title: Langø-dæmningen: anlægget i 1911
claims.claim: Familieerindringen daterer byggestarten til 11. januar 1911 og beskriver en dæmning på 334 meter. Den overordnede historie er omtalt af lokalarkivet, men myndighedsforløb, ansvar og præcis anlægsdato bør dokumenteres.
claims.evidence: Familieerindringen daterer byggestarten til 11. januar 1911 og angiver 334 meter. Erling Mortensen, De viste vejen (1969), s. 91, giver uafhængig historisk corroboration: Marius Christensen og familie udførte hovedparten af dæmningsarbejdet i 1911; han overtog Langø i 1894 for 4.000 kr.; dæmningen gik over 530 alen vand og blev anslået til 5.000–10.000 m³ jord. Bogen omtaler desuden en ministeriel resolution efter konflikt med fiskerne. Langeland Byarkivs register til Øboer 2011 bekræfter købet i 1894, 334 m dæmning og landfast forbindelse i 1911.
claims.missing: Den ministerielle resolutions dato, myndighed, journalnummer og fulde ordlyd; samtidige aviser; byggeregnskaber eller vej-/landvæsensakter. Den sekundære 1969-bog gengiver ikke selve resolutionen.
claims.next: Find den ministerielle resolution omtalt i De viste vejen s. 91. Søg i Ministeriet for Landvæsenets/Indenrigsministeriets journalsager samt Svendborg Amts og Humble Sogneråds arkiver 1910–1912; brug Marius Christensen, Langø, Humble, fiskernes indsigelse og dæmningsarbejdet som søgeord. Find også Lisbeth Skovs artikel “Langø og dæmningen” i Øboer 2011.

research_notes.title: Langø purchase and causeway
research_notes.context: 5. Holgersen / Christensen / Langø
research_notes.text:
Family memoir “En Langø-piges erindringer” says Marius and Ane Marie bought Langø in Lindelse Nor in 1894 for 4,000 kroner, with 1,600 kroner paid down, and moved there with four children. It says Marius and his sons began building the causeway to Kædeby Haver on 11 January 1911; it was eventually 334 metres long and 6–8 metres wide. The memoir also describes earlier grazing use, a prior owner and a forced sale.

Langeland Byarkiv's catalogue independently confirms Lisbeth Skov's 2011 article “Langø og dæmningen”: Marius Christensen and Ane Marie bought Langø in 1894 and built the 334-metre causeway in 1911. The real-register and land-book material for Lindelse and Magleby (1790–2013) is the next route to verify title and transaction terms. The memoir's more detailed financial and personal narrative remains family testimony until checked against the deed, auction and land-book.

Sources and media:
- [Langø memoir, page 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sloev/tree/main/images/04-langoe-erindringer.jpg)
- [Langø memoir, page 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sloev/tree/main/images/02-langoe-erindringer-s2.jpg)
- [Langeland Byarkiv](https://www.langelandsarkiv.dk/)
- [Lindelse Nor background](https://da.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindelse_Nor) — contextual, not title evidence.

research_notes.title: New independent corroboration — Langø's causeway (16 November 2026)
research_notes.context: 14. Emigration: precise protocol references
research_notes.text:
A strong independent printed source has now been located: Erling Mortensen, *De viste vejen: Modtagere af Det kgl. danske Landhusholdningsselskabs sølvbægere 1804–1969* (Landhusholdningsselskabets Forlag, 1969), p. 91. The entry for Marius Christensen, Langø, Humble sogn, says:

- Marius Christensen and his family completed the main part of the causeway work in **1911**; three sons and a son-in-law helped.
- He had taken over Langø in **1894** for **4,000 kroner** (1,600 kroner down payment).
- The causeway crossed about **530 alen of water**, including about 300 alen of soft bottom; the estimated earth volume was **5,000–10,000 m³**.
- The work was described as a long-held dream; the book says a ministerial resolution went against the fishermen after a dispute when Christensen began building.

This is a substantial independent corroboration of the family account's central chronology and identity. It also yields a new archival lead: the **ministerial resolution** is a traceable government decision and may identify the responsible ministry, date, legal basis and any objections from local fishermen. The book is a retrospective secondary source, not the resolution itself; keep the claim open until the original administrative record is found.

A second corroborating route is Langeland Byarkiv's catalogue for Lisbeth Skov's article “Langø og dæmningen” in *Øboer* 2011. Its summary independently states that Marius and Ane Marie Christensen bought Langø in 1894 and that the island was connected to Langeland in 1911 by a 334 m causeway built with help from sons and son-in-law. The full article should be consulted for references and any oral-history details.

Sources:
- Erling Mortensen, *De viste vejen* (1969), p. 91: https://slaegtsbibliotek.dk/2023/935679.pdf
- Langeland Byarkiv, *Øboer* 2011 article register: https://byarkivet.langelandkommune.dk/boeger-brochurer/register-over-artikler-i-oeboer

**Assessment:** 1894 acquisition and 1911 causeway are now strongly supported by independent secondary/local-archive sources. The family recollection's precise start date of 11 January 1911, exact 334 m length and legal/administrative circumstances still need primary-source verification.

research_notes.title: 6. Jørgen Christensen and Bodil Margrethe — emigration
research_notes.context: 6. Jørgen Christensen and Bodil Margrethe — emigration
research_notes.text:
Jørgen Christensen (`p126`) and Bodil Margrethe Clausdatter (`p127`) are ancestors of Ane Marie Jørgensen. The family chart says they had nine children; the eldest son and youngest daughter stayed in Denmark, while the others emigrated to America. Jørgen and Bodil also reportedly emigrated and later returned to Denmark. Preserve the exact nine names and original birth details from the family chart/GEDCOM. Do not assume the family travelled together or that “America” necessarily means the United States.

Search Danish emigration protocols, passenger arrivals, US census, naturalization, marriage, death and local records. Rigsarkivet cautions that the Copenhagen police emigration protocols after 1868 cover people who purchased contract tickets through an emigration agent; independent travellers may be absent. Therefore, a negative protocol search alone is not evidence that a person did not emigrate.

research_notes.title: What the civil records say
research_notes.context: 2. Lorenz's paternity — central conflict
research_notes.text:
The Egernsund civil birth register, 1932 no. 4 (BSID 37658, image 125), records that Else Gedde Frederiksen, née Jensen, gave birth to Lorenz on 12 January 1932 at 05:30. A marginal note dated 11 July 1932 reportedly names landworker Wilhelm Krogh of Snogbæk as father, based on:
- a paternity declaration dated 5 April 1932;
- a court decision dated 10 June 1932.

The Broager Vestre baptism register, 1933 no. 1 (BSID 201141, image 112), names worker Peter Frederiksen and wife Else Gedde Jensen as parents and refers to a letter from the civil registrar dated 11 July 1932. Peter was Lorenz's social/stepfather and gave him his surname.

These sources establish what was officially declared/registered and what the church register recorded. They do not, without the underlying paternity case and further evidence, conclusively establish biological paternity.

research_notes.title: What the family account says
research_notes.context: 2. Lorenz's paternity — central conflict
research_notes.text:
The typed family document “Paula Mathilde Chrestle Gedde og Jens Jensens slægt” and the handwritten family chart identify farmer's son Sophus (Sofus) Petersen of Påkjær, Nybøl, as Lorenz's biological father. The account says Wilhelm Krogh accepted paternity and Peter Frederiksen raised Lorenz as his own. This is a family claim that conflicts with the official registration.

Sophus Petersen was born 28 June 1903 and died 24 August 1945. His baptism in Nybøl in 1903 no. 12 identifies his parents as farmer Peter Petersen and Anna Cathrine Marie Petersen. A family grave photograph gives the same dates and names Påkjær. The 1921 Nybøl census is useful for the household and farm context but does not prove Lorenz's paternity.

research_notes.title: Keep three roles separate
research_notes.context: 2. Lorenz's paternity — central conflict
research_notes.text:
| Role | Person | Current evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Registered/legal father | Wilhelm Krogh | Civil-register marginal note, paternity declaration and court decision reported; underlying file not yet inspected |
| Family-claimed biological father | Sophus Petersen | Family account and chart; disputed, not independently established |
| Social/stepfather | Peter Frederiksen | Church-book entry and family account |

Do not rewrite the biological father field as settled. The canonical data no longer sets `father: sofus` as a settled parent link. Both the official register's biological-father designation for Wilhelm and the family's biological-father claim for Sophus are retained as separate, disputed relationship assertions. The step/social father Peter remains a separate link. This prevents the visual tree and downstream exports from presenting either disputed biological claim as established.

research_notes.title: Archive route
research_notes.context: 2. Lorenz's paternity — central conflict
research_notes.text:
Rigsarkivet's current guidance says paternity cases from 1919–1970 generally began with police; disputed paternity was decided by civil court; maintenance/alimentation files are held by the county archive. The recommended first route is the county archive's alimentation journal/register and case file, followed by the civil court's paternity case list and judgment book, and then the police journal if needed. Search using Else Gedde Frederiksen/Jensen, Lorenz (born 12 January 1932), Wilhelm Krogh of Snogbæk, the 5 April declaration, 10 June decision and 11 July marginal-note dates.

**New archival finding — exact county archive and a date-boundary trap (researched 16 November 2026):**
- The official Rigsarkivet archive overview identifies both the **Sønderborg Amt archive (1920–1932)** and the **Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt archive (1920–1971)**. It says the Sønderjylland county archives are journal archives with registers and case files, and that the Aabenraa/Aabenraa-Sønderborg holdings include *alimentationssager*. The 1920–1935 journal/register/case-file finding aid is unprinted and must be consulted in the Aabenraa reading room; the overview specifically lists an internal handover register for the Sønderborg Amt archive.
- The same overview states that Aabenraa and Sønderborg counties were merged with effect from **1 April 1932**. The Egernsund birth occurred on 12 January 1932, but the paternity declaration and judgment cited in the marginal note are dated **5 April and 10 June 1932**, respectively. Therefore do not assume all three documents are filed under the same county archive creator: inspect both **Sønderborg Amt** (for the January birth / any opening record) and **Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt** (for the April–June 1932 declaration/judgment and later alimentation administration). Daisy's creator page labels Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt from 1933, while the archive overview gives the merger's effective date as 1 April 1932; treat the naming/transfer boundary as an archival catalogue issue to confirm with staff, not as settled from the catalogue label alone.
- The county archive is the best starting point, but the civil/police records remain separate possibilities: the 1932 county merger did **not** transfer police or court powers to the amtmand. Rigsarkivet's archive creator note explicitly says amtmen had no police or court powers after 1919. Use the civil court and police route if the county file does not contain the judgment or source references.
- The 1932 file is beyond the general 75-year access restriction described by Rigsarkivet, but availability of a particular file still needs confirmation in Daisy and with the archive.

**Daisy catalogue check — no individual 1932 case reference surfaced online (researched 16 November 2026):**
- Rigsarkivet's Daisy search instructions confirm that the search supports both archive creators and archive-series names, and that older terminology matters: *børnebidrag* was formerly called *alimentation*. Daisy recommends checking all series attached to a known creator and trying singular rather than plural series names.
- Publicly indexed Daisy material confirms the archive creator **Sønderborg Amt** has 1920–1932 holdings, but the searches available here did not expose a 1932 *Alimentationsjournal*, *Alimentationssager* or individual case entry for Wilhelm Krogh. A Daisy search result for Sønderborg Amt showed 1920–1932 poverty-related series, but that is not evidence that the paternity file is in those series.
- The official archive overview's *alimentationssager* description is a group-level description of the county journal archives, not a verified box or case number for this specific case. The printed finding aid by Hans Schultz Hansen (1998), pp. 11–86, is the next practical route for the Aabenraa/Aabenraa-Sønderborg material; the separate unprinted 1920–1935 finding aid and Sønderborg handover register must also be checked. No original case file or judgment has yet been located or read.
- Practical request to the Aabenraa reading room: ask staff to search the 1920–1935 journal registers and journals for **Else Gedde Frederiksen (also Jensen), Wilhelm Krogh, Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen, 5 April 1932 and 10 June 1932**, including the *alimentationssager* group and any cross-reference to the civil court. Ask them to check both Sønderborg Amt and Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt, and the handover register. If the index uses a different spelling or a journal number, obtain the full case reference before ordering the file.

**Jurisdiction trace — Gråsten, not Sønderborg (researched 16 November 2026):**
- The official Rigsarkivet archive overview says that after the 1923 adjustment, **Egernsund (in Broager parish) was transferred into Gråsten judicial district**. A contemporary administrative summary likewise places Egernsund under the Gråsten police district. This resolves the earlier uncertainty about the local court/police jurisdiction for Else's Egernsund residence: start with **Retten i Gråsten / Gråsten Civilret** for the 10 June 1932 judgment, and **Gråsten Politikreds** for the initial police record. It does not establish which court decided the matter if Wilhelm Krogh lived in a different district; Rigsarkivet notes that where parents lived in different judicial districts, separate interviews and cross-references may exist.
- Daisy's public catalogue lists Gråsten Civilret *Faderskabssager* only from **1962 onward** (and Gråsten Civilret *Retsbog for faderskabssager* from 1978 onward). Those named series therefore do **not** cover the 1932 judgment. The 1932 civil record may instead be in a general *sagliste* / *dombog* / *borgerlige sager* series, or may be referenced in the county's alimentation file. Do not order the post-1962 faderskab series expecting the 1932 case.
- For police, Daisy lists **Gråsten Politikreds — Register til politiprotokol (1920–1959)** and a **Rejsepolitiprotokol (1932–1962)**. It also lists a *Politiprotokol for Lundtoft- og Nybøl Herred* (1923–1929), which ends before Lorenz's birth and is not itself the 1932 record. The register to the police protocol is the promising entry point; ask the archive which 1932 Gråsten police protocol or journal survives and whether the register covers the relevant case.
- Rigsarkivet's current guidance says the civil route is a *Sagliste for faderskabssager* (or general civil *Sagliste*) followed by the corresponding *Dombog*. The Daisy results surfaced no Gråsten-specific faderskab series for 1932, so ask staff to identify the equivalent general civil series for 1932 and check the date 10 June. The judgment may also be cited by case number in the alimentation file.
- Search terms remain Else Gedde Frederiksen/Jensen, Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen, Wilhelm Krogh (Snogbæk), and dates 5 April, 10 June and 11 July 1932. The father's residence may point to a second district; confirm Wilhelm's exact 1932 address before treating Gråsten as the only court.

Official guidance and finding aids:
- [Rigsarkivet — paternity and adoption cases](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/faderskab-og-adoption/faderskabssager-kom-godt-i-gang/)
- [Landsarkivet for Sønderjylland archive overview](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Landsarkivet-for-Soenderjylland-En-arkivoversigt.pdf)
- [Daisy — Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt archive creator](https://daisy.rigsarkivet.dk/arkivskaber_detaljer?a=&b=&c=b%C3%B8rnehjem&d=1&dir=a&e=2016&ed=&ep=&es=&f=&faid=&g=&gsc=he&h=&heid=14334077&henid=14334077&int=&m2rid=&meid=&ngid=709207&ngnid=&side=1&sort=3)

research_notes.title: Further catalogue tracing: 1932 Gråsten police paternity records
research_notes.context: 16. Broager / Nybøl / Rinkenæs collateral records and name traps
research_notes.text:
A second DAISY pass materially improves the police-archive route. The catalogue lists **Politiprotokol for faderskabsager, 1920–1976** under both:
- **Aabenraa Politikreds / Åbenrå Politi** (creator's official period 1920–1973; catalogue series 1920–1976): [DAISY creator and series overview](https://daisy.rigsarkivet.dk/arkivskabers_arkivserier?a=&b=&c=politi&d=1&dir=a&e=2016&ed=&ep=&epid=&es=&f=&faid=&g=&gsc=he&h=&heid=&henid=&int=&m2rid=&meid=&ngid=723322&ngnid=723324&side=1&sort=3).
- **Gråsten Politikreds** (the successor creator, officially 1973–2006; its catalogue nevertheless lists the same 1920–1976 paternity-protocol series, plus a separate *Faderskabsprotokol* for 1963–1976): [DAISY Gråsten creator and series overview](https://daisy.rigsarkivet.dk/arkivskabers_arkivserier?a=&b=&c=&d=&dir=a&e=&ed=&ep=&epid=&es=&f=&faid=&g=&gsc=&h=&heid=&henid=&int=&m2rid=&meid=&ngid=723236&ngnid=&side=1&sort=2).

This is stronger than the earlier generic Gråsten *Politiprotokol* / *Register til politiprotokol* route. The duplicated 1920–1976 series under both creators may reflect archival transfer or catalogue arrangement; it does **not** yet prove that a 1932 Gråsten case survives or identify its box/volume. Ask Rigsarkivet to check the 1932 section and determine whether Gråsten/Egernsund cases are indexed by mother's name, alleged father's name, or case number. The Gråsten creator overview also shows a separate *Faderskabsprotokol* only from 1963, so that later series is not the target.

Aabenraa's catalogue separately lists *Alimentationsjournal* (1920–1950), *Navneregister til alimentationsjournal* (1920–1950), and *Politiprotokol for faderskabsager* (1920–1976). These are additional leads, but Aabenraa's county/city jurisdiction should not be presumed to cover Egernsund. Ask whether the Aabenraa name register or journal cross-refers cases handled by Gråsten police, and whether the shared catalogue series is a merged or duplicated archival description.

Sources:
- [Aabenraa Politics archive overview, DAISY](https://daisy.rigsarkivet.dk/arkivskabers_arkivserier?a=&b=&c=politi&d=1&dir=a&e=2016&ed=&ep=&es=&f=&faid=&g=&gsc=he&h=&heid=&henid=&int=&m2rid=&meid=&ngid=723322&ngnid=723324&side=1&sort=3)
- [Gråsten Politics archive overview, DAISY](https://daisy.rigsarkivet.dk/arkivskabers_arkivserier?a=&b=&c=&d=&dir=a&e=&ed=&ep=&epid=&es=&f=&faid=&g=&gsc=&h=&heid=&henid=&int=&m2rid=&meid=&ngid=723236&ngnid=&side=1&sort=2)
- [Gråsten Politics register and police-protocol catalogue listing](https://daisy.rigsarkivet.dk/arkivskaber_eller_arkivserie_liste?a=&b=&c=politi&d=1&dir=a&e=2016&ed=&ep=&epid=&es=&f=&faid=&g=&gsc=he&h=&heid=3914051&henid=3914051&int=&m2rid=&meid=&ngid=5195068&ngnid=5195086&side=1&sort=2)

research_notes.title: Wilhelm Krogh's 1932 residence: unresolved
research_notes.context: 16. Broager / Nybøl / Rinkenæs collateral records and name traps
research_notes.text:
This research pass did not locate an independently verifiable census or directory entry for Wilhelm/Vilhelm Krogh at Snogbæk in 1932. The birth-register marginal note's description “landarbejder Wilhelm Krogh, Snogbæk” remains the only presently documented residence clue in this dossier. Do not treat Snogbæk as proof that he was resident in Broager parish on the precise date of the declaration, nor merge him with the separate Carl Vilhelm Krogh 1908 candidate or Detlef Krogh 1905 candidate.

The exact address and employer remain important because Rigsarkivet's guidance warns that when the parents lived in different judicial districts, interviews and file references can be split across districts. The next useful work is to identify the relevant Krogh household in the 1930 census and contemporary parish/address records, then use that residence to test whether any second police/court district must be searched. No original paternity file has yet been located or inspected.

research_notes.title: County archive route now takes priority (1932)
research_notes.context: 16. Broager / Nybøl / Rinkenæs collateral records and name traps
research_notes.text:
Rigsarkivet's current guidance for 1919–1970 says the case began with police, but recommends searching the county archive first because its *Alimentationsjournal* and related file often contain the civil court's paternity case. The county file can be found through an *Alimentationsjournal*, an ordinary journal, and the corresponding *Alimentationssager/Journalsager*. Only if that route fails should the court and police be pursued. [Rigsarkivet: Faderskabssager – Kom godt i gang](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/faderskab-og-adoption/faderskabssager-kom-godt-i-gang/).

For Egernsund, the dates straddle the 1 April 1932 county-administration transition:
- Sønderborg Amt archive covers 1920–1932.
- Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt archive covers 1920–1971; the official creator description explains that Aabenraa and Sønderborg came under the same amtmand in 1932 while retaining separate county council districts. The catalogue creator is officially named Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt from 1933, but the archive's holdings begin in 1920.
- The official archive overview identifies *Alimentationssager* as a normal county archive file group. It says the 1920–1935 journal-register/journal/file finding aid is unprinted and available in the reading room; the printed guide by Hans Schultz Hansen (1998), pp. 11–86, covers Aabenraa Amt 1920–32 and Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt 1932–72. Sønderborg Amt's own pre-merger holdings have a separate unprinted handover list.
- The 5 April 1932 paternity declaration and 10 June 1932 court decision therefore make it essential to check the transition-era Sønderborg and Aabenraa-Sønderborg finding aids, not simply assume one continuous county file.

The 1930 census is a practical way to identify Wilhelm Krogh's household/address: Rigsarkivet says Sønderjylland census records after 1920 are filed among the national rural-district/town census series and are available as scanned images through Arkivalieronline up to 1940. I have not yet found a name-indexed 1930 entry for Wilhelm Krogh/Snogbæk; this is an access route, not a claimed identification.

Practical request for Rigsarkivet Aabenraa reading room:
1. Consult the printed Schultz Hansen finding aid (1998), pp. 11–86, and the unprinted 1920–1935 journal-register/journal/file finding aid for the 1932 *Alimentationssager* and *Journalsager*.
2. Check both Sønderborg Amt 1920–1932 and Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt 1920–1971 holdings, paying particular attention to 1932 transition entries and whether the 5 April declaration, 10 June judgment or 11 July registrar letter is indexed under Else Gedde Jensen, Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen, Wilhelm Krogh or a journal number.
3. Ask whether the case file includes or cross-references the Gråsten Civilret decision and the Gråsten police investigation; if the county register has no entry, use the Gråsten paternity police protocol (1920–1976) and general civil registers.

Sources:
- [Rigsarkivet paternity case guide](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/faderskab-og-adoption/faderskabssager-kom-godt-i-gang/)
- [Rigsarkivet, Landsarkivet for Sønderjylland archive overview (PDF)](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Landsarkivet-for-Soenderjylland-En-arkivoversigt.pdf)
- [DAISY: Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt archive creator details](https://daisy.rigsarkivet.dk/arkivskaber_detaljer?a=&b=&c=b%C3%B8rnehjem&d=1&dir=a&e=2016&ed=&ep=&es=&f=&faid=&g=&gsc=he&h=&heid=14334077&henid=14334077&int=&m2rid=&meid=&ngid=709207&ngnid=&side=1&sort=3)
- [Rigsarkivet census guide](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/folketaellinger-kom-godt-i-gang/)

No 1930 census identification, county journal number or original paternity case file has yet been obtained. These remain research targets, not findings.

research_notes.title: 1930 census and correction to county search priority (16 November 2026)
research_notes.context: 16. Broager / Nybøl / Rinkenæs collateral records and name traps
research_notes.text:
A fresh check of Rigsarkivet's current paternity guide corrects the previous emphasis on the mother's Egernsund county archive. For cases of this period, Rigsarkivet says the paternity case was generally handled in the **county where the alleged father lived**; only when the father's name/address is unknown does it recommend starting with the mother's county. Thus Wilhelm Krogh's residence is the key jurisdictional fact. If Snogbæk is confirmed as his residence in 1932, the Sønderborg county archive remains the likely county route; if the 1930/1932 address points elsewhere, the relevant father's county must be checked instead. The county transition issue (Sønderborg Amt versus Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt after 1 April 1932) matters only after the father's county is established.

The 1930 census route is real but not yet completed:
- Arkivalieronline has a dedicated **Folketællinger, Sønderjylland** collection and the Landsarkivet for Sønderjylland's original census series (1769–1935). The series index is image-based; the online catalogue does not provide a name-searchable transcription for the target household.
- Independent local-history/genealogy indexes cite the **5 November 1930 census for Broager Sogn, Nybøl Herred, Sønderborg Amt**, including household/family references such as *skema 82, familie nr. 1*. This confirms that a Broager 1930 census exists and is cited by researchers, but does not identify Wilhelm Krogh.
- Search variants should include Wilhelm/Vilhelm, Carl Vilhelm, Krogh/Krog, and the place Snogbæk/Snogbaek. The candidate names already noted elsewhere in this dossier remain unmerged until the household and birth details match.

Practical next step: inspect the 5 November 1930 Broager census by locality/household, starting with Snogbæk, then compare any Krogh entry with the 1908 birth candidates and with the birth-register marginal note. If there is no matching household in Broager, widen to nearby Sottrup, Nybøl, Dybbøl and Gråsten, and then to the county implied by any alternative address.

Sources:
- [Rigsarkivet: Faderskabssager – Kom godt i gang](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/faderskab-og-adoption/faderskabssager-kom-godt-i-gang/) (explicitly says the case was generally handled in the father's county; mother's county is the fallback if father is unknown).
- [Arkivalieronline: Folketællinger, Sønderjylland](https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/da/other/other-collection/48)
- [Arkivalieronline: Landsarkivet for Sønderjylland, Originale folketællinger 1769–1935](https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/da/other/index-creator/48/14962499/20597409)
- [Broager Sogn overview and census guide](https://wiki.slaegt.dk/index.php/Broager_Sogn)
- [Local genealogy index citing the 1930 Broager census, skema 82](https://www.stroemming.dk/genealogy/gedweb/Public/da/Lists/placename-I.html)

No Krogh household has yet been identified in the 1930 census, and no exact address or employer has been established. The local genealogy index is a navigation aid, not evidence for Wilhelm's identity.

research_notes.title: Correct Arkivalieronline route for the 1930 Broager census (16 November 2026)
research_notes.context: 16. Broager / Nybøl / Rinkenæs collateral records and name traps
research_notes.text:
The previous census note pointed to the Sønderjylland special collection and the Landsarkivet's *Originale folketællinger* index. Rigsarkivet's own census guide gives a more precise route for this period: **after 1920, Sønderjylland's censuses are filed in the national census series under rural districts (*landdistrikter*) and market towns (*købstæder*)**, not in the special pre-1920 Sønderjylland census collection. The 1930 national series includes a dedicated *Folketælling 1930, Sognelister* selection page with fields for Amt, Kommune/Herred and Sogn.

Use this route:
1. Open [Arkivalieronline — Folketælling 1930, Sognelister](https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/da/rif/select/7/16972563).
2. Select **Sønderborg Amt** → **Nybøl Herred** (or the corresponding kommune/herred option offered by the selector) → **Broager Sogn**.
3. Inspect the schedule images locality by locality, beginning with Snogbæk; search handwritten spellings and the variants Wilhelm/Vilhelm, Carl Vilhelm, Krogh/Krog.
4. If Broager is negative, repeat for the nearby parishes indicated by the place-name evidence rather than assuming Snogbæk belongs to Broager parish.

The selector page is a navigation form, not a searchable name index; no Wilhelm Krogh household has been read or identified yet. This corrects the earlier implication that the 1930 Broager material might need to be located through the Landsarkivet's special original-census index. The special collection remains relevant for older Sønderjylland censuses, but is not the preferred route for this 1930 search.

Sources:
- [Rigsarkivet census guide — after 1920, Sønderjylland is under the national rural/town census series](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/folketaellinger-kom-godt-i-gang/) (section “Særlige forhold i Sønderjylland”).
- [Arkivalieronline — 1930 parish lists selector](https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/da/rif/select/7/16972563).
- [Arkivalieronline — 1930 census series listing](https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/da/rif/rif-collection/7).

No census household, exact address or employer has yet been verified; this update records the corrected archive route only.

research_notes.title: Follow-up: Sottrup census evidence and the 1932 Sønderborg court route (16 November 2026)
research_notes.context: 16. Broager / Nybøl / Rinkenæs collateral records and name traps
research_notes.text:
The new Vester Snogbæk identification is supported as a real place/parish combination by independent local census references. A published biography of Hans Jørgen Andresen explicitly cites the 5 November 1930 census for **V. Sottrup parish, Snogbæk**, held at Rigsarkivet. Strømming's genealogy index also cites 1930 census entries for several households in Snogbæk, Sottrup parish, including the Petersen household at matrikel Snogbæk 18. These references establish the correct census locality and that the 1930 schedules are used by researchers; they do **not** identify Wilhelm or his family. The public K-name index's only Krogh entry is an unrelated Anne Marie Krogh, so it is not a usable name index for Wilhelm.

The photo leads need to be kept separate:
- Arkiv.dk search results list an undated item “1870–1900 Præstevænget 1, Nybøl, Detlef Krogh” and another “1927–1944 Detlef Krogh, Joller, Præstevænget 1, Nybøl”.
- A local-history publication about Bachmann's brickworks names a Detlef Krogh among workers photographed in 1930.
These could be valuable visual leads, but the Præstevænget/Nybøl address is not the stated Vester Snogbæk address, and none of the image captions establishes whether the person is Wilhelm's proposed father (b.1876), brother (b.1905), or another Detlef Krogh. Do not use them to merge identities.

**Court/police catalogue refinement:** a DAISY search for the exact series name “faderskabssager” finds the following Sønderborg-specific holdings:
- Sønderborg Politi: *Journal vedr. faderskabssager* only **1944–1945**.
- Retten for Sønderborg Købstad / Sønderborg Købstads Civilret: *Journal for faderskabssager* **1944–1957**, *Retsbog for faderskabssager* **1946–1957**, and later dedicated *Faderskabssager* series. These start too late for the 1932 decision.
- However, DAISY lists a general **Retsliste for borgerlige retssager** for Sønderborg Købstads Civilret covering **1920–1957**. This is now the best catalogued court entry point for the 10 June 1932 decision: ask staff to search the 1932 retsliste by the names Wilhelm Krogh, Else Gedde Jensen and Lorenz Frederiksen, and then trace any case number to the corresponding general civil judgment/protocol.
- The dedicated Gråsten *Politiprotokol for faderskabsager* is catalogued from 1920–1976, so it remains a possible source for the mother's-side investigation, even though the alleged father's proposed Sottrup address points to Sønderborg.

This confirms why the district split matters: the father-side 1932 civil case may be in Sønderborg's general civil court records, while interviews or police work concerning Else in Egernsund may be in Gråsten. Do not assume the later dedicated paternity series cover 1932 simply because the catalogue has a similar title for later years.

Next action is to inspect the **1930 Sottrup parish schedules**, not Broager, and ask Rigsarkivet for the 1932 Sønderborg civil *retsliste* and associated judgment records. If the case is not in the Sønderborg retsliste, test the Gråsten general civil court registers as the mother's-side alternative.

Sources:
- [Hans Jørgen Andresen biography, citing 5 November 1930 census at V. Sottrup, Snogbæk](https://denstorekrig1914-1918.dk/soenderjyder-oversigt/soenderjyder-a/andresen-hans-joergen-1891-1973/).
- [Strømming: Kristen Petersen, Snogbæk, Sottrup — 1930 census citation](https://www.stroemming.dk/genealogy/gedweb/Public/da/Details/Details-I383.html) (unrelated household; locality confirmation only).
- [Arkiv.dk search listing, including Detlef Krogh photo captions](https://arkiv.dk/soeg?page=2&searchstring=krogh%2C+hans).
- [Local-history publication: Bachmann brickworks workers in 1930](https://slaegtsbibliotek.dk/2025/953685.pdf).
- [DAISY exact-series search: faderskabssager](https://daisy.rigsarkivet.dk/arkivserie_liste?a=&b=faderskabssager&c=&d=1&e=2024).
- [DAISY: Retsliste for civil cases, including Sønderborg Købstads Civilret 1920–1957](https://daisy.rigsarkivet.dk/arkivskaber_eller_arkivserie_liste?c=retsliste&d=1&e=2019).
- [Trap 5: Nybøl Herred — court and police district changes](https://trap5.lex.dk/herred/nyboel-herred-soenderborg-amt/).

No Krogh household has yet been read in the original Sottrup 1930 census, and no 1932 court case number has been found. These remain the next record targets.

research_notes.title: Sottrup 1930 census search: access confirmed, no Krogh household yet (16 November 2026)
research_notes.context: 16. Broager / Nybøl / Rinkenæs collateral records and name traps
research_notes.text:
A fresh check of Rigsarkivet's current census guide confirms that **all Danish census material through 1940 is scanned and viewable on Arkivalieronline**. For Sønderjylland after 1920, the guide specifically directs researchers to the national census series under landdistrikter/købstæder. The correct 1930 series is *Folketælling 1930, Sognelister*; its selector has fields for Amt, Kommune/Herred and Sogn and explains that the schedules list households with names, ages, household roles, occupations and (from 1845) birthplaces.

Direct route: [1930 census parish-list selector](https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/da/rif/select/7/16972563). Select Sønderborg Amt, Nybøl Herred and Sottrup Sogn. The selector is interactive and its selected image references are not exposed in the text-search index, so this research pass did not retrieve or read the Snogbæk schedule images themselves. **No claim is made that Wilhelm is absent from the original census.**

Independent locality cross-checks:
- A biography for Hans Jørgen Andresen cites the 5 November 1930 census in Sottrup Sogn, specifically Vester Sottrup.
- Strømming's public genealogy index cites 1930 census entries for Snogbæk, Sottrup Sogn.
- Arkiv.dk search results identify a 1920–1930 image as “Snogbæk præstegård, Vester Snogbæk 6”. This corroborates the Vester Snogbæk place-name, not a Krogh residence.
- Searches of indexed web material for “Wilhelm Krogh”/“Vilhelm Krogh” with Snogbæk or Sottrup did not surface a census entry. This is only a failure to find an indexed transcription; the original census is not name-searchable through the selector.

A separate Strømming all-names index result for **Elisabeth Andersdatter** records her baptism at Sottrup in 1713 and death at Snogbæk in 1756. This is unrelated to the Krogh family but confirms Snogbæk as a historical locality within Sottrup Sogn.

**Practical next step:** open the 1930 parish-list selector and inspect the Sottrup schedules image by image, locating the Snogbæk/Vester Snogbæk section. Transcribe all Krogh/Krog households and neighbouring farmhands, including variant first names. If the images are numerous, first locate the locality headings or schedule numbers using the 1930 Sottrup census citations in the local-history biographies, then inspect adjacent schedules. Follow any identified Wilhelm household back to the 1925 census and Adelby baptism register.

Sources:
- [Rigsarkivet census guide](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/folketaellinger-kom-godt-i-gang/) — confirms scanned access through 1940 and the post-1920 Sønderjylland filing route.
- [Arkivalieronline: 1930 parish-list selector](https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/da/rif/select/7/16972563).
- [Hans Jørgen Andresen biography](https://denstorekrig1914-1918.dk/soenderjyder-oversigt/soenderjyder-a/andresen-hans-joergen-1891-1973/) — census reference for Sottrup, 5 November 1930.
- [Strømming: Kristen Petersen, Snogbæk, Sottrup](https://www.stroemming.dk/genealogy/gedweb/Public/da/Details/Details-I383.html) — unrelated household, census locality reference only.
- [Arkiv.dk: Snogbæk præstegård, Vester Snogbæk 6](https://arkiv.dk/soeg?searchString=%20b%C3%B8rnehavel%C3%A6rer) — place-name/photo caption, not a Krogh record.
- [Strømming all-names index](https://www.stroemming.dk/genealogy/gedweb/Public/da/Lists/allnames-A.html) — historical Sottrup/Snogbæk locality reference.

No Krogh household, 1930 address, 1908 baptism or 1932 court case number has been confirmed in this pass. The family-tree supplement's proposed parents and siblings remain secondary leads only.

research_notes.context: Revised first route for the 1932 paternity case: county archive before court (16 November 2026)
research_notes.text:
Rigsarkivet's current guidance for 1919–1970 explicitly recommends starting with the county archive: the alimentation/maintenance file often also contains the civil court's paternity case. If no county file is found, search the civil court; if that fails, search the police. This supersedes the earlier court-first ordering in this dossier. The case's recorded dates (declaration 5 April 1932, decision 10 June 1932, marginal note 11 July 1932) provide a narrow search window.

For the father's proposed 1932 residence at Vester Snogbæk, Sottrup Sogn, the first county target remains Sønderborg Amt. For the mother's Egernsund residence, keep the Gråsten-side locality and any cross-referenced police/court records in view. Rigsarkivet says that when parents lived in different judicial districts, interviews would typically occur in each district with cross-references. The 1932 administrative transition is a complication: the official archive overview lists separate Sønderborg Amt holdings for 1920–1932 and Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt holdings for 1920–1971; the overview states the 1920–1935 finding aid for registers, journals and case files is unprinted and available in the reading room. The Daisy description for Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt notes that the two counties came under the same amtmand in 1932 but retained separate county council districts, and that the amtmand's administration increasingly handled social and family-law matters including paternity. Do not assume that the new joint administration means the case must be filed under the later joint archive title: ask staff to check both the Sønderborg Amt and transition-era Aabenraa-Sønderborg holdings, with the 1 April 1932 boundary in mind.

research_notes.text:
Ask Rigsarkivet Aabenraa to search the Sønderborg Amt and transition-era Aabenraa-Sønderborg county archive registers/journals for an alimentation or paternity matter concerning:
- Child: Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen, born 12 January 1932 in Egernsund.
- Mother: Else Gedde Jensen, resident Egernsund (Gråsten judicial/police district).
- Named/acknowledging father: Wilhelm/Vilhelm Krogh, landworker, resident Vester Snogbæk, Sottrup (Sønderborg judicial/police district).
- Declaration: 5 April 1932; reported civil court decision: 10 June 1932; civil-register marginal note: 11 July 1932.
- Search variants: Krogh/Krog; Wilhelm/Vilhelm; Else Gedde Jensen; Lorenz Frederiksen.
Request the journal number, the relevant Alimentationssag/Journalsag, and any enclosed copy or reference to the civil court decision. If the county register does not identify the matter, proceed to the Sønderborg Købstads Civilret general *Retsliste for borgerlige retssager* (1920–1957) for 1932, then the corresponding general civil judgment book and case file. The Daisy catalogue confirms that this general retsliste series exists for the relevant period; the dedicated Sønderborg court paternity journal and judgment-book series begin later and therefore are not the right 1932 starting point. Only after these should we request Gråsten/Sønderborg police registers and protocols.

Sources:
- Rigsarkivet, “Faderskabssager – Kom godt i gang,” 1919–1970 route and cross-district procedure: https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/faderskab-og-adoption/faderskabssager-kom-godt-i-gang/

research_notes.title: What is now firmly established as a research path
research_notes.context: Consolidation checkpoint: online evidence exhausted for the disputed 1932 paternity (16 November 2026)
research_notes.text:
1. **1930 census:** Rigsarkivet's national collection lists “Folketælling 1930, Sognelister”; its selector has Amt, Kommune/Herred and Sogn fields. The Sottrup schedule must be selected and read as original images, focusing on Snogbæk/Vester Snogbæk. No searchable name index is exposed on the selector. The collection describes household-by-household enumeration with names, ages, household positions and occupations. Sources: https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/en/rif/rif-collection/7 and https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/en/rif/select/7/16972563.
2. **1932 paternity:** The county-first request documented above is the appropriate archive route. There is no online evidence yet that identifies a case number or confirms the underlying ruling's full contents. The civil register's reported marginal note remains evidence of registered/legal paternity only; the family's claim for Sophus Petersen remains unproved.
3. **Adelby 1908:** Archion's current public list for Adelby exposes “Taufen 1882–1907” (local signature Adelby_2.3), not 1908. It does expose the Adelby marriage register “Trauungen 1884–1937” (Adelby_5.3), accessible through an Archion account. The archive's separate overview describes a wider baptism series through 1949, so an archive enquiry is needed for the 1908 continuation. Source: https://www.archion.de/de/alle-archive/schleswig-holstein/landeskirchliches-archiv-der-evangelisch-lutherischen-kirche-in-norddeutschland/kirchenkreis-schleswig-flensburg/adelby/273644.
4. **Nybøl Detlef:** The 1981 local-history register does list Detlef Krogh at holding no. 32, with the note “from 1883 only indersted.” It is a property-history lead, not an identification of the Detlef in Wilhelm's proposed family. The full PDF confirms the register title and that it is a Nybøl 1851 holdings list (printed p. 71): https://slaegtsbibliotek.dk/2025/953243.pdf.

research_notes.title: What would actually close the Lorenz branch
research_notes.context: Consolidation checkpoint: online evidence exhausted for the disputed 1932 paternity (16 November 2026)
research_notes.text:
The decisive missing item is the original 1932 paternity/alimentation file or the court case file. It should settle what Wilhelm acknowledged, what the court decided, and whether any biological evidence or statements naming another man survive. The 1930 census and Adelby church book are supporting identity checks, not substitutes for that file. Until the county archive/court file is obtained, this branch cannot honestly be marked solved.

**Triage decision:** online discovery for this branch is now exhausted enough that repeating broad web searches is unlikely to help. Keep it as a tightly specified archive retrieval task rather than letting it block the more promising ancestral lines. If the original case file is later obtained, revisit the biological-father question; otherwise retain the three distinct roles already documented (registered/legal father Wilhelm Krogh, family-claimed biological father Sophus Petersen, social father Peter Frederiksen) and do not collapse them into one.
