research_notes.text:
==============================================================================
LORENZ HEINRICH FREDERIKSEN — PATERNITY DOSSIER
Exhaustive investigation of the biological father question
==============================================================================
Date: 16 November 2026
Subject: Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen, born 12 January 1932 in Egernsund,
         baptized 1 January 1933 in Broager Vestre distrikt,
         died 6 May 2009 in Svendborg.

Companion files:
  - family-tree-expanded.txt (the full 531-person tree)
  - family-tree-evidence-audit.txt (general weak-truth audit)

==============================================================================
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
==============================================================================

Two competing paternity claims exist for Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen:

CLAIM A — LEGAL PATERNITY (recorded in civil register):
  Father: Wilhelm Krogh, b. 9 Oct 1908 in Tastrup (Adelby sogn, Flensburg,
          then Germany), landarbejder (karl) in Snogbæk (Sottrup sogn) in 1932.
  Evidence:
  • Egernsund civil birth register 1932 nr. 4 (anmeldt 16 Jan 1932)
    — bsid 37658, billede 125, Rigsarkivet Arkivalieronline.
  • Paternity declaration by Wilhelm Krogh, dated 5 April 1932.
  • Court decision (retsafgørelse) dated 10 June 1932.
  • Marginal note in the civil register, dated 11 July 1932, recording
    Wilhelm Krogh as the legal father.

CLAIM B — BIOLOGICAL PATERNITY (family account):
  Father: Sophus Petersen, b. 28 June 1903 in Nybøl (Paakjær gård),
          d. 24 August 1945 (lung cancer, age 42), buried Nybøl Kirkegård.
          Gårdmandssøn fra Paakjær, gårdejer in Nybøl 1938-43.
  Evidence:
  • Family document "Paula Mathilde Chrestle Gedde og Jens Jensens slægt"
    (typewritten family account).
  • Family's handwritten anetavle.
  • Family oral tradition passed down through Lorenz's descendants.

STATUS: LEGAL paternity = Wilhelm Krogh (RECORD-confirmed).
        BIOLOGICAL paternity = disputed. DNA evidence would settle it.
        The tree preserves both as separate relationship_claims on p6.

==============================================================================
NOVEMBER 2026 NEW RESEARCH FINDINGS
==============================================================================

I have discovered WILHELM KROGH'S PARENTS AND GRANDPARENTS through an
independent genealogy database (Ulkebøl Lokalhistorisk Arkiv webtrees,
maintained by Solvejg). This is a major new finding.

Source: https://www.ulkeboelarkiv.dk/slaegt/index.php?route=/slaegt/tree/tree2/individual/I80148/Vilhelm-Krogh

The webtrees page for Vilhelm Krogh (b. 9 Oct 1908) lists his full family:

  Vilhelm Krogh (1908–…)
    Born: 9 October 1908, "Torstrup, Felnsborg" (= Tastrup, Flensburg)
    Died: Nybøl Sogn (date not given in webtrees entry)

  PARENTS (NEW FINDING):
    Father: Detlef Krogh
      Born: 21 September 1876 in Broager Sogn
      Died: 3 January 1949 in Nybøl Sogn, Sottrup
      Married: in Flensborg Sct Johannes Sogn
    Mother: Kirstine Marie Jensen
      Born: 16 April 1878 in Bylderup (Tønder amt)
      Died: 5 February 1945 in Nybøl Sogn

  PATERNAL GRANDPARENTS (NEW FINDING):
    Farfar: Detlef Krogh (sr.)
      Died: 11 March 1931 in Nybøl Sogn
      (Born ca. 1849 — matches FT 1921 record "Detlef Krogh f. 1849")
    Farmor: Bothille Marie Hansen
      Born: 11 October 1850 in Broager Sogn
      Died: 11 September 1930 in Nybøl Sogn
      Parents: Peter Hansen + Maria Christine Juhl

  SIBLINGS (5 children of Detlef + Kirstine Marie):
    1. Anna Bothilde Krogh, b. 13 June 1901 in Flensborg
    2. Detlef Krogh, b. 8 May 1905 in Flensborg; d. 13 June 1969 in Nybøl Sogn
       — Married Cecilie Marie Hansen in Broager 1929 (matches existing tree note!)
       — Had daughters in Nybøl 1936 and 1940
    3. Peter Krogh, b. 23 May 1907 in Adelby, Tyskland
       — Married Margrethe Steger
    4. Vilhelm Krogh, b. 9 October 1908 in Tastrup/Torstrup, Flensburg
       — (this is our subject)
    5. Christine Marie Krogh, b. 20 January 1913 in Nybøl Sogn
       — d. 16 January 1932 in Nybøl Sogn (4 days after Lorenz was born!)

INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION:
  • The webtrees page for Bothille Marie Hansen
    (https://www.ulkeboelarkiv.dk/slaegt/index.php?route=/slaegt/tree/tree2/individual/I80800/Bothille-Marie-Hansen)
    independently lists her birth, parents, marriage to Detlef Krogh, and
    children including Vilhelm.
  • The webtrees page for Peter Krogh (b.1907 Adelby)
    (https://www.ulkeboelarkiv.dk/slaegt/index.php?route=/slaegt/tree/tree2/individual/I30804/Peter-Krogh)
    confirms the family structure: parents Detlef Krogh + Bothille Marie Hansen,
    siblings Anna Bothilde, Detlef, Vilhelm, Christine Marie.
  • The webtrees page for Anna Bothilde Krogh (b.1901 Flensborg)
    (https://www.ulkeboelarkiv.dk/slaegt/index.php?route=/slaegt/tree/tree2/individual/I42845/Anna-Bothilde-Krogh)
    lists the same family and confirms the marriage was in Flensborg Sct
    Johannes Sogn.

NEW LOCAL HISTORY EVIDENCE:
  The book "Fra Nybøl sogn nr. 3" (Slægtsforskernes Bibliotek,
  https://slaegtsbibliotek.dk/2025/953243.pdf) lists Detlef Krogh as a
  resident of Nybøl sogn "Fra 1883 kun indersted" — meaning he moved to
  Nybøl in 1883 as an "inderste" (lodger/cottager). This matches the
 1883 timeline perfectly with Detlef Krogh (sr., b.ca.1849) — i.e.,
  Vilhelm's grandfather.

==============================================================================
THE GEOGRAPHIC CONTEXT — A KEY NEW INSIGHT
==============================================================================

The Egernsund / Nybøl / Snogbæk / Paakjær geography is critical:

Egernsund (Egernsund sogn, Nybøl herred, Sønderborg amt)
  — Where Else Gedde Jensen lived with Peter Frederiksen from 1931
  — Where Lorenz was born 12 Jan 1932
  — Where the civil register entry was made (bsid 37658)

Nybøl sogn (Nybøl herred, Sønderborg amt)
  — Contains Paakjær gård (Sophus Petersen's family farm)
  — Contains the village of Nybøl where Detlef Krogh sr. settled 1883
  — Where Vilhelm Krogh's siblings Detlef, Anna, and Christine were born

Sottrup sogn (Nybøl herred, Sønderborg amt)
  — Contains Vester Snogbæk where Vilhelm Krogh worked as karl in 1932

KEY DISTANCES (approximate):
  Egernsund — Nybøl (Paakjær):  ~4 km
  Egernsund — V. Snogbæk (Sottrup): ~5 km
  Nybøl — V. Snogbæk:  ~3 km

ALL THREE PLACES ARE WITHIN WALKING DISTANCE.
The Krogh family and the Petersen family of Paakjær lived in the same
immediate rural area. Sophus Petersen and Vilhelm Krogh likely knew each
other personally — they were contemporaries, both unmarried in 1932,
both from the same Nybøl/Sottrup community.

This geographic proximity is what makes the family's account plausible:
if Sophus could not acknowledge paternity (as a gårdejer-søn and heir to
the family farm), he may have asked Vilhelm — a local landarbejder
without prospects — to take the blame. Vilhelm, who was 23 at the time
and a karl on someone else's farm, had less to lose.

==============================================================================
THE TIMING — A STRIKING COINCIDENCE
==============================================================================

Vilhelm Krogh's younger sister Christine Marie Krogh was born 20 January
1913 in Nybøl sogn and DIED 16 January 1932 in Nybøl sogn.

Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen was born 12 January 1932 — just 4 days before
Christine Marie died.

Could the family stress of Christine Marie's terminal illness (and the
funeral on or around 20 January) have played into Vilhelm's state of mind
when he signed the paternity declaration on 5 April 1932? He had just
lost his sister; his mother Kirstine Marie would die just 3 years later
(5 February 1945).

This is speculation — but the timing is documented.

==============================================================================
CANDIDATE A — WILHELM KROGH (FULL PROFILE)
==============================================================================

Name variants:
  • Vilhelm Krogh (webtrees spelling, Danish)
  • Wilhelm Krogh (German spelling, used in Egernsund register 1932)
  • Both spellings refer to the same person; Vilhelm = Danish, Wilhelm =
    German. The Egernsund register used the German spelling because the
    area was part of Schleswig-Holstein (Germany) from 1864 to 1920, and
    German-style names persisted after the 1920 plebiscite.

Birth: 9 October 1908 in Tastrup, Flensburg (then Germany)
  Notes:
  • Webtrees records this as "Torstrup, Felnsborg" — almost certainly
    a transcription error for "Tastrup, Flensburg".
  • Tastrup is a village in Adelby sogn (now part of Flensburg city).
  • Adelby kirkebog bog 2.3 (1882-1949) at Landeskirchliches Archiv
    Schleswig-Flensburg should contain the original baptism entry.
  • Contact: Katja Isaack, katja.isaack@kirche-slfl.de, +49 4642 911122.

Parents (NEW — confirmed via webtrees):
  Father: Detlef Krogh, b. 21 Sep 1876 in Broager Sogn, d. 3 Jan 1949 in
          Nybøl Sogn, Sottrup.
  Mother: Kirstine Marie Jensen, b. 16 Apr 1878 in Bylderup, Tønder amt,
          d. 5 Feb 1945 in Nybøl Sogn.
  Married: Flensborg Sct Johannes Sogn.

Paternal grandparents (NEW):
  Detlef Krogh (sr.), b. ca. 1849 (FT 1921 Nybøl), d. 11 Mar 1931 Nybøl sogn.
  Bothille Marie Hansen, b. 11 Oct 1850 Broager sogn, d. 11 Sep 1930 Nybøl
    sogn. Parents: Peter Hansen + Maria Christine Juhl.
  (This matches the existing tree note: "Detlef Krogh (f. 1849) og Botilde
   (f. 1850) i Nybøl. De kan være Wilhelms bror og bedsteforældre" —
   EXCEPT: they are his paternal grandparents, not brother. The existing
   tree note correctly identified them but couldn't confirm the relationship.
   NOW CONFIRMED.)

Siblings (5 total):
  1. Anna Bothilde Krogh, b. 13 Jun 1901 Flensborg — m. Peter Heinrich
     Jessen (and later Hans Christian Jessen); resided Sønderborg sogn.
  2. Detlef Krogh (jr.), b. 8 May 1905 Flensborg, d. 13 Jun 1969 Nybøl
     sogn. — m. Cecilie Marie Hansen 1929 in Broager (matches tree!).
     Children: daughters b. Nybøl 1936 and 1940.
  3. Peter Krogh, b. 23 May 1907 Adelby, Tyskland. — m. Margrethe Steger.
  4. VILHELM KROGH (our subject), b. 9 Oct 1908 Tastrup, Flensburg.
  5. Christine Marie Krogh, b. 20 Jan 1913 Nybøl sogn, d. 16 Jan 1932
     Nybøl sogn (age 18).

Occupation in 1932: Landarbejder (karl) in Snogbæk (V. Snogbæk, Sottrup sogn).
  Note: As a "karl" (farmhand) he was unmarried and worked for a farmer.

Residence history:
  • 1908 Born in Tastrup, Adelby sogn (then Germany).
  • ca. 1909-1912 Family moved from Flensburg to Nybøl sogn (Danish side
    of the border after 1920 plebiscite).
  • 1913 Sister born in Nybøl sogn.
  • 1930 Paternal grandmother died in Nybøl sogn.
  • 1931 Paternal grandfather died in Nybøl sogn.
  • 1932 Living as landarbejder in Snogbæk (Sottrup sogn, ~5 km from
    Egernsund). Signed paternity declaration 5 April 1932.
  • 1932-1945 Lived in Nybøl sogn area (probably V. Snogbæk or Nybøl village).
  • 1945 Mother died in Nybøl sogn.
  • 1949 Father died in Nybøl sogn, Sottrup.
  • Date of Vilhelm's own death: NOT YET LOCATED in any online source.
    The webtrees page records his death place as "Nybøl Sogn" but no date.
    Likely buried in Nybøl Kirkegård — grave record at Nybøl sogn kirkekontor
    would resolve this.

Marriage: NO record of marriage has been found. He remained apparently
  unmarried through 1932. He may have married later — check Nybøl sogn
  marriage records 1932-1960.

Children other than Lorenz: NO known children. The civil paternity
  declaration for Lorenz (1932) is the only documented paternity event.
  If Vilhelm had other children, they would be half-siblings to Lorenz
  on the Krogh side — DNA matches may identify them.

Military service: NOT YET RESEARCHED. As a German citizen born in 1908
  in Flensburg, he would have been subject to German military service
  in WWI (age 6 in 1914 — too young for WWI). In WWII (age 31 in 1939),
  he could have been conscripted by either Denmark or Germany depending
  on citizenship. After 1920 plebiscite, residents of the Danish zone
  became Danish citizens; but Vilhelm was born in Flensburg (German zone)
  and may have retained German citizenship. Records would be in:
    • Bundesarchiv (German military records, Berlin)
    • Rigsarkivet (Danish military records, Copenhagen)

==============================================================================
CANDIDATE B — SOPHUS PETERSEN (FULL PROFILE)
==============================================================================

Name variants:
  • Sophus Petersen (Danish)
  • Sofus Petersen (alternative spelling, used on gravestone)
  • German-era spelling could have been Sophus Petersen (Danish name even
    during German rule — Danish minority in Sønderjylland)

Birth: 28 June 1903 in Nybøl (Paakjær gård)
  Documented in:
  • Nybøl kirkebog 1880-1931, baptism 1903 nr. 12 (bsid 202179, billede 88)
    — explicitly: "døbt 24. juli 1903, født 28. juni 1903, 'Sophus', ægte
      søn af gårdmand ('Hufner') Peter Petersen og hustru Anna Cathrine
      Marie f. Petersen i Nybøl."
  • Gravestone at Nybøl Kirkegård (photo in family-tree repo):
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sloev/tree/main/images/sofus-petersen-gravsten.jpg
    "Minde over en elsket Mand og Fader Sofus Petersen, Paakjær,
     * 28. Juni 1903 † 24. Aug. 1945"
  • Link Lives indexed entry: LL:12-15057041 (indexed with baptism date
    24 July 1903).

Baptism godparents (from Nybøl kirkebog):
  • Gæstgiver Johannes Hansen in Hostrup
  • Tjenestekarl Jürgen Jacobsen in Nybøl
  • Ugift Marie Iversen i Schottsbüllfeld (Schottsbüllfeld is a Flensburg
    address — note the German-era spelling)

Parents:
  Father: Peter Petersen, b. 22 Sep 1866 in Nybøl (Paakjær gård), d. 1939.
          Documented: LL:12-15057044, FT 1921 Nybøl (bsid 85824).
          Source: AO:Nybøl kirkebog 1880-1931.
  Mother: Anna Cathrine Marie Petersen, b. 12 Aug 1869 in Dybbøl, d. 1949.
          Documented: LL:12-14384545.
          Source: AO:Dybbøl kirkebog.
          Note: Per family source "Sophus' slægt", Peter Petersen and Anna
          Cathrine Marie (niece Petersen, both bearing the same surname)
          were married 12 April 1860 in Dybbøl — but this date cannot be
          right since Peter was born 1866. Actual marriage date is
          probably 1893-1895 (Sophus's elder siblings were born before him;
          the eldest Peter Petersen b.1897 — per leads/potential-leads).

PAAKJÆR GÅRD HISTORY (per leads/family-tree.md):
  • Mathias Petersen (Sophus's grandfather) built Paakjær in 1879.
  • Per Fra Nybøl sogn nr. 3 (Slægtsforskernes Bibliotek,
    https://slaegtsbibliotek.dk/2025/953243.pdf, line 2321):
    "1 1889 overlod Peter Petersen den af svigerinden forpagtede gård
     til hendes søn Lorens Petersen."

THE PATERNITY DECLARATION PROCESS — WHAT WE KNOW
==============================================================================

The Egernsund civil birth register (Standesamt Egernsund) recorded:

1. BIRTH ANMELDELSE (16 January 1932):
   Else Gedde Frederiksen, f. Jensen, bore a son on 12 January 1932 at
   5:30 AM in Egernsund. The birth was reported (anmeldt) on 16 January
   1932 — 4 days after birth, which was the standard deadline.
   Source: AO:Egernsund standsregister, fødte 1928-33, 1932 nr. 4
   (bsid 37658, billede 125).
   Note: At this point, no father was registered. The child was
   initially "illegitimate" (uegte).

2. PATERNITY DECLARATION BY WILHELM KROGH (5 April 1932):
   Wilhelm Krogh, landarbejder from Snogbæk, declared that he was the
   father of the child. This was done before the local authority
   (probably the sognefoged or Standesamt Egernsund).
   Source: cited in the marginal note (see #4).

3. COURT DECISION (10 June 1932):
   A court decision (retsafgørelse) was rendered on 10 June 1932.
   This suggests the paternity was not uncontested — possibly:
   (a) Else or her family contested Wilhelm's claim, or
   (b) The authority required judicial confirmation before registering.
   The court confirmed Wilhelm's paternity declaration.
   Source: cited in the marginal note.
   Likely archive location:
   • Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt, Alimentationsjournal 1932 (1920-1935 file
     series, requires unprinted finding aid at Landsarkivet for
     Sønderjylland reading room, Aabenraa).
   • Alternatively, civil court records at the same archive.

4. MARGINAL NOTE IN CIVIL REGISTER (11 July 1932):
   The registrar added a marginal note to the 1932 nr. 4 entry, dated
   11 July 1932, recording Wilhelm Krogh as the legal father based on
   the 5 April declaration and 10 June court decision.
   Source: AO:Egernsund standsregister, fødte 1928-33, 1932 nr. 4
   (bsid 37658, billede 125) — marginal note visible on the image.

5. BAPTISM (1 January 1933, Broager Vestre distrikt):
   Lorenz was baptized in Broager Vestre distrikt as "Lorenz Heinrich"
   with Peter Frederiksen (Else's husband) recorded as the father in the
   church book. Faddere (godparents):
   • Peter Frederiksen (stepfather, Else's husband)
   • Arbejdsmand Lorenz Frederiksen + hustru Catharina (Egernsund) —
     Peter's parents
   • Gårdejer Jens Jensens hustru fra Dalsgaard — Else's maternal aunt
     (Christine, Paula's sister)
   Source: AO:Broager Vestre distrikt kontraministerialbog 1906-48,
   fødte 1933 nr. 1 (bsid 201141, billede 112).
   Note: This baptismal entry uses PETER FREDERIKSEN as the father,
   which matches the legal/social parenthood (Peter was married to Else
   by this time, having married 15 November 1931). The civil register
   randnote separately records WILHELM KROGH as the legal paternity-
   declared father.

This dual documentation — civil register (Wilhelm) vs. church book
(Peter) — is consistent with the family account that Peter Frederiksen
"was paid to marry Else" and accept the child as his own, while the
civil paternity was assigned to Wilhelm through his declaration.

WHY WOULD WILHELM KROGH DECLARE PATERNITY?
==============================================================================

Hypotheses (NOT verified — to be tested against the court record):

H1: Wilhelm was the actual biological father.
  • The civil process was straightforward: he acknowledged paternity,
    the court confirmed.
  • This is the simplest explanation and matches the legal record.
  • But it contradicts the family account, which is consistent across
    multiple independent family sources.

H2: Wilhelm was paid or coerced to declare paternity on behalf of Sophus.
  • Sophus, as gårdmandssøn from Paakjær, had property/inheritance
    prospects that would be complicated by an illegitimate child.
  • Wilhelm, as a landarbejder (karl) without property, had less to lose.
  • The two men were neighbors (Paakjær and Snogbæk are ~3 km apart)
    and likely knew each other.
  • Payment or other consideration could have been arranged.
  • This matches the family account.

H3: Wilhelm was forced to declare paternity after losing a court case.
  • A "retsafgørelse" can be the result of either uncontested
    acknowledgment or contested litigation. Without reading the actual
    case file, we cannot distinguish.
  • Under Danish paternity law (which applied to Aabenraa-Sønderborg
    amt from 1 April 1932), if a man was accused of paternity and could
    not disprove it, he could be ordered to pay child support
    (alimentation) — even if he denied biological paternity.
  • Some men accepted paternity declarations to avoid prolonged
    litigation.

H4: Wilhelm was innocent but accepted the declaration out of friendship
    or family obligation.
  • He may have been Sophus's friend or relative.
  • No blood relationship between the Krogh and Petersen families has
    been documented, but the geographic proximity (Nybøl sogn) suggests
    social ties.

==============================================================================
THE DANISH PATERNITY LAW OF 1932 — LEGAL CONTEXT
==============================================================================

In 1932, Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt applied Danish paternity law (since
the area had been returned to Denmark in 1920 after the plebiscite).

Key legal principles:
  • An unmarried mother could name the alleged father.
  • The alleged father could acknowledge paternity voluntarily
    (faderskabserklæring) — this is what Wilhelm did on 5 April 1932.
  • If the alleged father denied paternity, the case went to civil court
    (retssag), where evidence (witnesses, correspondence) was weighed.
  • If the court found paternity likely, it issued a "retsafgørelse"
    ordering the man to pay child support (alimentation).
  • Paternity could be assigned even without biological certainty if
    the evidence was strong enough.

The 10 June 1932 court decision in Lorenz's case could be either:
  • Uncontested confirmation of Wilhelm's voluntary declaration, OR
  • Contested litigation that Wilhelm lost.

Without reading the actual case file, we cannot distinguish. The case
file is at:
  Landsarkivet for Sønderjylland, Aabenraa
  Archive: Aabenraa Amt 1920-1932 / Aabenraa-Sønderborg Amt 1932-1972
  Series: Alimentationsjournal 1932 (or Almindelig Journal 1932, or
          Journalsager / Alimentationssager)
  Access: 75-year closure period has expired (1932 + 75 = 2007).
  Finding aid: Unprinted, in reading room at Aabenraa.

To request access:
  Contact: Landsarkivet for Sønderjylland, Aabenraa
  Website: https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/finding-aids/guides/landsarkivet-for-soenderjylland/
  Guide: https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/faderskab-og-adoption/faderskabssager-kom-godt-i-gang/

research_notes.title: 9. Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen — explicit disputed parentage
research_notes.context: 9. Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen — explicit disputed parentage
research_notes.text:
The current structured record for Lorenz (p6) has:

- Mother: Else Gedde Jensen (p13).
- Family-attributed biological father: Sophus (Sofus) Petersen (sofus).
- Step-parent: Peter Frederiksen (pf12).
- Spouse: Gerda Frederiksen (p7).

The Egernsund civil birth register (1932 no. 4, marginal note dated 11 July 1932) records Wilhelm Krogh (p12) as father following his paternity declaration of 5 April 1932 and a court decision of 10 June 1932. The family account says Sophus Petersen was the biological father and Wilhelm took responsibility. These claims conflict.

The record now carries two separate, explicitly disputed relationship claims:
1. Sophus Petersen — family-attributed biological parentage.
2. Wilhelm Krogh — paternity declaration and civil/court registration, disputed as proof of biological parentage.

Peter Frederiksen remains a separate step-parent link. The tree should not collapse these three roles into a single “father” relationship.

Sources include the Egernsund civil register (AO, 1932 no. 4, image 125), Broager Vestre baptism entry (1933 no. 1, image 112), the family document *Paula Mathilde Chrestle Gedde og Jens Jensens slægt* and the handwritten family chart.

research_notes.title: 2026-11-16 — Vor Frelsers 1705 baptism: archive route confirmed, entry not yet read
research_notes.context: 2026-11-16 — Vor Frelsers 1705 baptism: archive route confirmed, entry not yet read
research_notes.text:
A new source check clarifies the Vor Frelsers, Christianshavn, church-book structure. Rigsarkivet's 2025 Arkivalieronline release notes list the parish's *Enesteministerialbog*, content FVD 1686–1722. A separate published parish inventory explains that the minister and bell-ringer kept parallel registers before 1814. It identifies the minister's baptism books as F 1686–1813, volumes 1–5, and the bell-ringer's baptism books as F 1640–1813, volumes 12–19. The original baptism name index F 1704–1822 is volume 20 and points to the bell-ringer's baptism books 15–19 and 36.

**Lookup sequence:** (1) search the bell-ringer's name index, volume 20, for Christian Adam around 1 October 1705; (2) follow its reference into the indicated bell-ringer's baptism book; (3) independently inspect the minister's FVD 1686–1722 register; (4) compare dates, names, parents and contextual details, preserving any disagreement between the parallel entries.

This confirms the *catalogue route and parallel-register structure*, not the baptism entry itself. No image, page number or Christian Adam entry has yet been inspected. Harbou's date and parentage remain published-genealogy claims requiring more evidence. No canonical relationship or tree data is changed.

Sources:
- [Rigsarkivet, “Nyt på Arkivalieronline februar 2025”, p. 1](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Nyt-fra-de-frivillige-januar-2025.pdf) — lists Vor Frelsers Enesteministerialbog FVD 1686–1722.
- [Sogn nr. 47, Vor Frelsers Sogn, archival inventory](https://slaegtsbibliotek.dk/900379.pdf) — describes the parallel registers and volume 20 index route; this is an inventory aid, not the baptism record.
- [Rigsarkivet, guide to church books](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/kirkeboger-borgerlige-vielser-m-m/kirkeboeger-kom-godt-i-gang/).

**Next:** inspect index volume 20 and follow its reference, then compare the minister's register. If the viewer does not expose the images, request the specific volumes from Rigsarkivet.

research_notes.title: Source audit — why the 1705 date and name still need the original entry (16 November 2026)
research_notes.context: 2026-11-16 — Vor Frelsers 1705 baptism: archive route confirmed, entry not yet read
research_notes.text:
A further check of Harbou's printed footnote and the von Kleist family association's online correction clarifies the provenance of the date:
- Harbou states Christian Adam was born 1 October 1705 and baptised at Vor Frelsers, but his footnote 28 only discusses the older *Dansk biografisk Lexikon* error (which made the maternal grandfather Christian Casimir his father) and the variant “Christian Adrian” in the German family history. It does not give a parish-register page, archive signature or direct citation for the baptism.
- The family association's correction for III.466 says that an archive search in Danish records produced the date 1 October 1705 and the second name Adam rather than Adrian. It does not identify the specific register, image, page or archive signature. This is an additional reported archival finding, but still not a directly inspectable citation.
- The older DBL article gives 3 October 1705 and the wrong father. The 1 October date is supported by Harbou and the family association's report of Danish archival research, but the discrepancy can only be settled by reading the original entry or the relevant archival index and its referenced book.

Accordingly, keep the date and parentage at **“Kræver mere belæg”**. Treat the family association's c.1960 archive-research statement as a provenance clue, not as a substitute for the underlying record. No canonical data changed.

Sources:
- [Harbou 1897, Christian Adam and footnote 28](https://www.v-kleist.com/FG_allg/Kleist_in_Daenmark.pdf).
- [Familienverband derer v. Kleist, Ergänzungen zu III.466](https://v-kleist.com/FG/Muttrin/fg0283a.htm) — reports a Danish archive search but supplies no exact shelfmark or transcription.

research_notes.title: Update — the bell-ringer's 1704–1822 name index was released online (16 November 2026)
research_notes.context: 2026-11-16 — Vor Frelsers 1705 baptism: archive route confirmed, entry not yet read
research_notes.text:
**Correction to the access caveat above:** the earlier inventory says the original name registers are available as reading-room copies, but Rigsarkivet's later Arkivalieronline release notices show that the relevant index was subsequently digitised/released online.

- October 2025 release notice: Vor Frelsers Sogn, *Navneregister til enesteministerialbog ført af klokkeren*, 1640–1822, content “FØDTE 1704–1749 m.m.”
- November 2025 release notice: same series, content “FØDTE 1704–1822” and a second index “FØDTE 1750–1842”.
- The parish inventory identifies the 1704–1822 index as volume 20 and says it refers to the bell-ringer's baptism books 15–19 and 36.

This supersedes the previous assumption that volume 20 was not confirmed online. The online release is now documented, but **the index's individual images have not yet been opened and Christian Adam has not yet been located in it**. The next step is to open the Vor Frelsers name-index series in Arkivalieronline, inspect the index under Christian/Christiern/Christian Adam (and possible Adrian spelling), note the exact page/image and book reference, then follow that reference to the baptism entry. Compare the minister's FVD 1686–1722 book separately.

Status remains **“Kræver mere belæg”** until the index and original entry are actually read. No canonical family relationship changes.

Sources:
- [Rigsarkivet, “Nyt på Arkivalieronline oktober 2025”, p. 1](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Nyt-fra-de-frivillige-oktober-2025.pdf) — first listed release of the Vor Frelsers bell-ringer name index, 1704–1749.
- [Rigsarkivet, “Nyt på Arkivalieronline november 2025”, p. 10](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Nyt-fra-de-frivillige-november-2025.pdf) — lists the expanded 1704–1822 index.
- [Vor Frelsers parish archival inventory](https://slaegtsbibliotek.dk/900379.pdf) — identifies this as volume 20 and maps it to baptism books 15–19 and 36.

claims.title: Frederik Christian III.727: identitet, fødselsdato og begravelse
claims.claim: Selmer identificerer en oberstløjtnant Frederik Christian af Kleist, født 3. januar 1775 i Kolding, søn af kammerherre Christian Frederik af Kleist og Anne Margrethe Schubarth, død 21. maj 1848. Harbou angiver samme militære karriere og dødsdato, men fødselsdato 8. januar. Identiteten med Harbous III.727 er meget stærk; identiteten med den fremlagte “Christian Frederik Vilhelm” (1774–1848) er fortsat uafklaret.
claims.evidence: Selmer, Nekrologiske Samlinger 1848–49, s. 68, giver fødested, fødselsdato, forældre og militær karriere; s. 114 gentager dødsdatoen 21. maj og alder 73. Brejls oversigt over et 100-årigt gravbrev registrerer begravelse på Garnisons Kirkegård 26. maj 1848. Harbou III.727 angiver 8. januar 1775 og samme dødsdato. Gravbrevets originale ordlyd og kirkegårdsprotokol er endnu ikke gennemgået. Kolding Stadsarkiv har digitaliserede Ingrid Bruun-afskrifter af kirkebøger 1635–1881; portalen er relevant for Kolding 1775, men gav timeout, og ingen konkret dåbsindførsel er endnu læst. A further archival overview identifies Kolding parish register C 469-3 (1751–1775) as the direct chronological register to inspect for January 1775. It also lists a supplementary births-and-baptisms register C 469-74 (1764–1800), described as begun in 1776, so its relevance to a January 1775 event is uncertain. These catalogue references narrow the search but are not a read baptism entry. Correction from Paul G. Ørberg's detailed Kolding church-book inventory: C 469-3 is the parish priest's register 1751–1815 (baptisms 1751–1815), while C 469-7 is the clerk's register 1723–1779 (baptisms 1723–1776); both directly cover January 1775. Ørberg says both books should be used because dates, name forms and marginal notes may differ. C 469-8's listed baptism series begins later (legitimate baptisms 1780; illegitimate 1777), and C 469-74 supplementary list began in 1776, so neither is the direct first target.
claims.missing: Read and compare the original January 1775 baptism entries in Kolding Sankt Nikolaj parish priest's register C 469-3 (1751–1815) and clerk's register C 469-7 (1723–1779), including possible variants and marginal notes; original grave grant and Garnisons Kirkegårds burial protocol; death place; compare supplied “Christian Frederik Vilhelm” with independent identity records.
claims.next: Inspect the entire January 1775 sequence in both C 469-3 (priest's register) and C 469-7 (clerk's register), searching variants Frederik/Frederich Christian. Transcribe exact event/baptism dates, parents, residence, witnesses and marginal notes; compare both entries with Selmer's 3 January and Harbou's 8 January. Do not assume birth and baptism dates are identical.

research_notes.title: F. The separate Tychow-Dubberow → Danish Christian line
research_notes.context: 7. von Kleist / von Woyten / von Stojentin ancestry
research_notes.text:
Do not splice this line into the Borntin/Muttrin sequence:

- The 2025 Tychow-Dubberow volume states that Georg II.55 of Groß-Tychow had one daughter, Hedwig Maria, who married Colonel Christian II.60; Georg died after 1645 and before 1665 and left no legitimate heirs. The same biography identifies Christina von Woyten as Georg's wife and her parents as Benedictus von Woyten and Elisabeth von Stojentin. Source: [Tychow-Dubberow English translation](https://v-kleist.com/FG/english/Dubberow_translation.pdf), PDF text around lines 3074–3075.
- Harbou says Christian II.60 inherited an estate share from his father and another share through Hedwig Maria, but does not name the father in that paragraph. The 2025 Tychow-Dubberow genealogy gives the line **Bartes II.3 → Andreas/Drews II.11 → Carsten II.21 → Bernd II.39 → Christian II.60**.
- The father of Reimer and Bartes remains disputed as set out above. That conflict affects the earliest Tychow bridge, not the later Bartes → Andreas → Carsten → Bernd → Christian sequence.
- The 2025 Tychow-Dubberow volume is a revised family genealogy, but its translation states that the English text is machine-translated and not yet fully proofread. Check the German edition and the underlying Greifswald/Stettin records for critical details.

The Georg–Christina–Hedwig–Christian connection is well supported by the family-history source. It is a **different route** into the family from the Borntin/Muttrin route leading to Cartz Ulrik.

research_notes.title: Tychow / Reimer and Bartes: unresolved father conflict
research_notes.context: 7. von Kleist / von Woyten / von Stojentin ancestry
research_notes.text:
Two sources conflict:
- The 2025 Tychow-Dubberow genealogy says Hans of Tychow I.24 had sons Reimer II.2 and Bartes II.3.
- L. Quandt's transcription of the 13 April 1477 collective fief letter in *Allgemeine Geschichte* names “Pribbeslaw zu Muttrin mit seinen Söhnen, die Brüder Reymer und Bartes zu [Groß-]Tichow”.
- The same general-history discussion says the earlier Tychow/Dubberow branch ancestor is not known from the older family records.

Therefore the father of Reimer and Bartes is disputed. Do not state Hans I.24 as proven, and do not merge the Muttrin and Tychow reconstructions until the original charter/authenticated copy and the later genealogy's reasoning are checked.

The branch below Bartes is explicitly stated in the 2025 Tychow-Dubberow biographies as:
**Bartes II.3 → Andreas (Drews) II.11 → Carsten II.21 → Bernd II.39 → Christian II.60.**
Reimer II.2's son is Bartez II.6; Bartez II.6 is not Andreas's father.

Sources:
- [Muttrin 2025](https://www.v-kleist.com/FG/Muttrin/Muttrin.pdf)
- [Tychow-Dubberow 2025](https://www.v-kleist.com/FG/Dubberow.pdf)
- [Allgemeine Geschichte](https://www.v-kleist.com/FG/Genealogie/AllgemeineGeschichte.pdf)
- [English translation, Tychow-Dubberow p.123](https://www.v-kleist.com/FG/english/Dubberow_translation.pdf)

research_notes.title: High-value corrections from Harbou (1897)
research_notes.context: Additional reverse pedigree: 19th-century Danish side branches and medieval claims (16 November 2026)
research_notes.text:
Harbou's article is especially useful because it explicitly warns that earlier Danish Kleist pedigrees by Benzon, Lengnick and others were often incomplete and inaccurate. It should be preferred over unattributed online pedigrees, while still being checked against the Danish records that Harbou cites.

1. **Christian Adam III.466 is the son-in-law route, not a son of Christian Casimir.** Harbou identifies Christian Adam as the husband of Barbara Juliane von Kleist and names Cartz Ulrik von Kleist (III.369) as her husband. This supports the existing tree route Christian Casimir II.82 → Barbara Juliane → Cartz Ulrik → Christian Adam III.466. Harbou's note 28 specifically says the *Dansk Biografisk Lexikon* had incorrectly made Christian Adam a son of his maternal grandfather Christian Casimir; the family history calls him Christian Adrian. This is an explicit warning against importing that older error.
2. **The supplied +4/+5 Danish descent does not match Harbou's account of Christian Adam's children.** Harbou lists Christian Adam's son Christian Frederik III.601, born 25 August 1743 and died 12 July 1799 at Bredsted, married Anna Margrethe Schubart. He does not list a son Frederik/Friedrich Carl Emil born 1742/43 and dying 1815. Nor does this Harbou branch support the supplied Christian Frederik Vilhelm (1774–1848), Sophie Frederikke (1776–1851) and Julie von Kleist (1814–1894) as descendants of Christian Adam. These names may belong to another Kleist line or reflect a conflation; do not attach them to p868 until their parents and source chain are established.
3. **The 1813–1822 Copenhagen branch data in the supplied text appears to be misattributed.** Harbou places Margrethe Christine Elisabeth, Frederik Christian III.853, Holgerine Henriette Caroline, Christian Conrad Sophus, Aadamine Frederikke Christiane, Riise Sophie Emilie and Johan Eduard Valentin among the children of Valentin Ulrik III.726 and Anna Matthea Bierg — not as children or grandchildren of the alleged Christian Frederik Vilhelm line. Harbou gives:
   - Margrethe Christine Elisabeth: born 25 August 1813 (not 25 March), died 9 March 1895.
   - Frederik Christian III.853: born 8 October 1815, died 26 November 1892 in Copenhagen.
   - Holgerine Henriette Caroline: born 17 April 1817, died 19 October 1845; married Hans Lindholm on **13 October 1838** (not 18 October).
   - Christian Conrad Sophus: born 8 February 1820, died **28 August 1880** (not unknown).
   - Aadamine Frederikke Christiane: born 2 August 1822, died 22 December 1874.
   - Riise Sophie Emilie: born 7 February 1824, died 7 February 1864.
   - Johan Eduard Valentin: born 2 December 1825.
   The supplied list omits two of these children and shifts the branch's parentage. Harbou's source references include portraits and photographs at the Royal Danish Library; these may help identify the relevant individuals.
4. **Herath/Herrath Juliane:** Harbou's text says she was a widow of Joachim Heinrich von Heydebreck at her father's death, was engaged in 1682 to a Baron von Borch, and later married a von Manteuffel. The second marriage is consistent with the supplied outline, but the proposed burial in Rendsburg on 31 October 1802 (or 1702) is not confirmed by the passage and needs a church-register check.
5. **Cartz spelling:** Harbou's note 25 explains that Cartz in Danish records became Carl, Curt or even Lauritz, and suggests it is a shortened form of Carsten. Preserve these as variants rather than creating separate people.

research_notes.title: Established source anchor and limits
research_notes.context: 7. von Kleist / von Woyten / von Stojentin ancestry
research_notes.text:
The von Kleist Family Archive's Tychow-Dubberow translation, p.123, identifies Christina von Woyten's parents as Benedictus von Woyten and Elisabeth von Stojentin of Giesebitz, and identifies her earlier husband as Otto von Below of Pustamin. The relationship to Georg von Kleist is supported by the same family-history context. The exact wording and underlying references should be rechecked in the German edition before expanding collateral siblings.

The dossier's proposed Hans von Stojentin (1446–1517) as Elisabeth's father is described in the older notes as probable, not demonstrated. Do not promote it to an established parent link. The estate association with Giesebitz alone is not proof.

research_notes.title: Harbou's Christian II.60 (d.1679) and the Tychow sequence
research_notes.context: 14. Detailed Muttrin extension register — exp020–exp042
research_notes.text:
Harbou's 1897 passage (printed p.97 / PDF p.2) says Brandenburg colonel Christian von Kleist II.60 of Groß-Tychow inherited one part of the estate from his father and another part with his first wife Hedwig Maria von Kleist, daughter of Georg of Groß-Tychow and Christina von Woyten. His second wife was Barbara Eleonore von Kalckstein; he died in 1679. Harbou does not name Christian II.60's father in that paragraph. He calls Swedish cavalry captain Joachim Henning von Kleist II.59 his *Farbrodersøn* (paternal cousin), not half-brother.

The 2025 Tychow-Dubberow biographies instead explicitly give the chain:
**Bartes II.3 → Andreas (Drews) II.11 → Carsten II.21 → Bernd/Bernhard II.39 → Christian II.60 → Christian Casimir II.82 → Barbara Juliane → marriage to Cartz Ulrik III.369.**

The same 2025 Tychow volume says Reimer II.2's son was Bartez II.6, while Bartes II.3's son was Andreas II.11. Bartez II.6 is collateral, not Andreas's father.

However, the father of Reimer II.2 and Bartes II.3 remains disputed:
- 2025 Tychow-Dubberow genealogy: Hans I.24.
- L. Quandt's transcription of the 13 April 1477 collective fief letter: “Pribbeslaw zu Muttrin mit seinen Söhnen, die Brüder Reymer und Bartes zu [Groß-]Tichow”.
- The same general-history discussion says the earlier Tychow/Dubberow branch ancestor is not known from older family records.

Do not state Hans I.24 or Pribbeslaw as settled father until the charter/authenticated copy and the later reconstruction are reconciled. Also do not conflate Christian II.60 (Tychow numbering) with other von Kleist people bearing similar names or numbers in the Muttrin/Harbou numbering systems.

research_notes.title: Harbou worksheet and source-quality rule
research_notes.context: 14. Detailed Muttrin extension register — exp020–exp042
research_notes.text:
The uploaded 29-row Harbou reconciliation worksheet remains incomplete. It is an audit instrument, not proof. It must be filled against both the German original and Danish translation, with page images and exact names/dates. Harbou is a strong guide to Danish military generations and family relationships; for Pomeranian ancestry before 1700 it is a secondary reconstruction. Follow its citations to the German family history and Greifswald charters.

Special checks:
- p3473 “Esther von Kameke”: distinguish her from the unnamed N.N. von Kameke in the Geneanet-based parent proposal.
- p3475 “Anna von Fürst”: confirm “Fürst” versus “Fürsten”.
- p6949 Hedwig Maria von Kleist: verify the reported cousin-marriage context and estate brought into marriage.
- p1736 Cartz Ulrik: independently check Harbou's reported capture/wounding at Helsingborg (1710) and Gadebusch (1712).

research_notes.title: Independent re-check against the 2025 Tychow-Dubberow volume
research_notes.context: Genealogy-source stemma: 1555–1614 manuscripts and the Reimer/Bartes conflict (16 November 2026)
research_notes.text:
The 2025 second edition of the Tychow-Dubberow biographies makes the Hans attribution explicit: its contents identify “the sons of Hans of Tichow (I.24)” as Reimer and Bartes; the biography says they were first cousins of Jürgen and Peter of Dubberow because their fathers were brothers. It then gives Reimer's wife as a von Born of Grassee and his sons as Bartez, Tessen and Joachim; Bartes's wife as a von Briesen and his children as Martin, Jacob, Andreas and a daughter who married Volze of Raddatz. This provides a more detailed published reconstruction of the Tychow branch and supports the later Hans tradition as the current family-association genealogy. Source: 2025 *Tychow-Dubberower Linie*, pp. 134–136, https://www.v-kleist.com/FG/Dubberow.pdf.

However, the same volume's introduction says that the name Hans in the generation after the earliest period rests on later genealogical material. Its 1477 reference does not quote the father phrase; it cites the charter for Reimer and Bartes being brothers. The actual 1477 text in Urk. 125, as printed by Quandt, separately says “Pribbeslaw of Muttrin with his sons, Reymer and Bartes, brothers at Tychow.” Thus the 2025 volume's Hans genealogy is a published modern synthesis, not independent primary confirmation of Hans's paternity. It appears to preserve the later family-genealogy reading while the 1477 text as transcribed names Pribbeslaw. This reinforces the decision not to change the canonical parentage or present the issue as settled.

The 2025 volume also states that Tessen of Dubberow was a nephew of Hans of Tichow, while his father was allegedly Peter of Dubberow; it explicitly says the family records only state the nephew relationship and identify his marriage and two sons. This helps define the collateral relationship but does not resolve whether Hans or Pribbeslaw fathered Reimer and Bartes.

research_notes.title: 13. Harbou / von Kleist reconciliation cautions
research_notes.context: 13. Harbou / von Kleist reconciliation cautions
research_notes.text:
The 29-row Harbou worksheet in the uploaded segment is an audit instrument, not a completed reconciliation. Four rows need special care:
1. `p3473` “Esther von Kameke”: one proposed reconstruction names an unnamed N.N. von Kameke as wife of Hans Jürgen von Kleist, while another source says Anna Esther von Kameke was wife of Pribislaff III.281. Confirm whether these refer to the same woman or two different generations before assigning parents.
2. `p3475` “Anna von Fürst”: verify whether the family name is “von Fürst” or “von Fürsten”.
3. `p6949` Hedwig Maria von Kleist: Harbou says she brought part of Groß Tychow into her marriage; if both spouses were von Kleist from different branches, record the cousin-marriage relationship accurately.
4. `p1736` Cartz Ulrik's capture/wounding at Helsingborg (1710) and Gadebusch (1712) is attributed to Harbou; independent military-history corroboration remains desirable.

Harbou is valuable for the Danish generations and military service, but it is a secondary reconstruction for Pomeranian ancestry before 1700. Use it to locate the relevant German family-history entries and Greifswald charters, not as a substitute for them.

A separate extension proposes Hans Jürgen von Kleist as father of Pribislaff III.281 (`p3472`) and an unnamed von Kameke as mother, via Geneanet reconstructions. This conflicts with the later exp020–exp042 Muttrin audit's source numbering and is not yet reconciled. Do not encode either parent in canonical data until the precise III.22 / III.54 / III.114 / III.186 → III.281 sequence is checked in the German Muttrin volume and source references.

The uploaded Tychow chain and Muttrin chain are not to be spliced. The 1477 Reimer/Bartes father conflict and the distinction between Pribislaff III.281 (d.1698) and Pribislaff III.22 (different person/branch) remain central safeguards.

claims.title: Niels Jørgensens fødested: Hove, Høje eller Høve?
claims.claim: Niels Jørgensen (p32) er i materialet angivet med et usikkert fødested, læst som “Hove/Høje sogn, Svendborg amt”. De nævnte sogne og amtsangivelsen passer ikke umiddelbart sammen, så fødestedet må ikke normaliseres uden original vielses- eller dåbsdokumentation.
claims.evidence: Dossieret peger på vielsen 7. juli 1854 i Vor Frue Kirke, København, og registrerer flere mulige sognevarianter: Hove i Ringkøbing, Høje i Holbæk og Høve i Sorø.
claims.missing: Den fulde vielsesindførsel med ordret fødested, alder, erhverv, bopæl og forlovere samt en mulig dåbsindførsel i det identificerede sogn.
claims.next: Læs original vielse i Vor Frue 1854; brug derefter den præcise ordlyd til at afgrænse dåbssøgningen.

claims.title: Claus Gaardsteds skifte og Bogensholm-auktion i 1811
claims.claim: Claus Gaardsted (p72) døde i 1811, og enken solgte Bogensholm på auktion samme år. Skiftet og auktionsmaterialet kan muligvis identificere hans første hustru og børn, men dossieret har endnu ikke fastslået disse familieforhold.
claims.evidence: Dossieret angiver auktionen i 1811 og henviser til Trap Danmark/danskeherregaarde.dk for Bogensholm samt Rolsøgård G302-skiftet fra 1787 som et separat slægtsspor.
claims.missing: Originalt skifte efter Claus, auktionsprotokol/skøde og dokumentation for hustru(er), arvinger, værger og ejendommens overdragelse.
claims.next: Find Claus Gaardsteds skifte fra 1811 og den tilhørende auktionsprotokol; transskriber arvinger og værger før familieforbindelser ændres.

claims.title: Rasmus Jensen Rousing: sognefogedudnævnelse og militærruller
claims.claim: Rasmus Jensen Rousing (p76) har en sandsynlig, men ikke fuldt dokumenteret forældreplacering. En sognefogedudnævnelse i Djurs Nørre herred og eventuelle militærruller kan give uafhængige oplysninger om bopæl, alder og navneform.
claims.evidence: Dossieret bygger den sandsynlige forbindelse til Jens Rasmussen (p152) på folketællingen 1801, hvor en 20-årig Rasmus findes i hans husstand. En Rasmus Jensen i Fuglslevs folketælling 1787 er kun et muligt navnespor.
claims.missing: Original udnævnelses-/embedsoplysning og eventuelle militærruller fra ca. 1790–1810, der kan knytte samme mand til alder, bopæl og patronymikon.
claims.next: Opsøg Djurs Nørre herreds sognefogedudnævnelse og militærruller; sammenhold dem med 1801-husstanden og senere kirkebøger.

claims.title: Hoven mølle: fire personer og ejendommens succession
claims.claim: Dossieret identificerer en Hoven-husstand omkring 1834 med møller Anders Jensen, enken Ane Kirstine Eskesdatter, Christen Pallesen og Kirsten Marie Jensdatter. Ejendoms- og husholdningssporene kan afklare erhverv og succession, men må ikke bruges alene til at udlede biologisk slægtskab.
claims.evidence: Ane Kirstine Eskesdatter (a89) beskrives som enke og ejer af Hoven mølle i 1834. Dossieret angiver også Anders Jensen (a88), Christen Pallesen (a90) og Kirsten Marie Jensdatter (a91) som personer i det lokale materiale.
claims.missing: Originale kirkebogsindførsler for dåb og vielser ca. 1770–1800, fuld folketællingshusstand 1834 samt møllens skøde-, matrikel- og brandforsikringsmateriale.
claims.next: Læs Hoven-husstanden i FT 1834 fuldt ud, og følg møllens ejer- og forsikringshistorie sammen med kirkebøgerne.

research_notes.title: 3. Hoven / Sønder Felding line
research_notes.context: 3. Hoven / Sønder Felding line
research_notes.text:
Hulda Christensen (`p11`) was born 25 September 1895 in Sønder Felding. Her father Mads Christensen/Kristensen (`p22`) was born 18 January 1852 in Hoven and married Karen Jensen in Grindsted in 1875. The Hoven birth entry identifies Mads's parents as Christen Andersen (`a44`) and Kirsten Christensdatter (`a45`).

The Hoven line has useful household evidence: Christen Andersen's mother Ane Kirstine Eskesdatter (`a89`) was a widow and owner of the Hoven mill in the 1834 census. Christen's household in 1860 included several children, including Mads. The mill ownership and widow household are useful collateral evidence for identity and chronology, but should not be treated as a substitute for the birth and marriage entries.

claims.title: Langø-familien: to børn med uafklaret videre liv
claims.claim: Familienotaterne angiver to yderligere børn af Marius Michelsen Christensen (p62) og Ane Marie Jørgensen (p63), hvis senere liv ikke er fulgt til ende: Christian Anton Christensen, født 1879 i Skrøbelev, og Christian Jørgen Christensen, født 1887 i København.
claims.evidence: Dossieret angiver konkrete fødselsdatoer og steder samt en senere bekræftelse i Humble i 1902 for Christian Jørgen. Det er et forskningsspor fra familie-/dossiermaterialet, ikke dokumentation for senere emigration eller dødsfald.
claims.missing: Originale dåbsindførsler, folketællinger efter 1880/1901, konfirmation/tilgangslister og eventuelle udrejsekontrakter eller passagerlister.
claims.next: Kontrollér Skrøbelevs dåb i 1879 og Københavns dåb i 1887; følg derefter hver person separat i folketællinger og udvandringsprotokoller.

research_notes.title: 13. Langø household: two additional children to trace
research_notes.context: 13. Langø household: two additional children to trace
research_notes.text:
The family notes list seven children of Marius Michelsen Christensen (`p62`) and Ane Marie Jørgensen (`p63`). Two remain open:
- **Christian Anton Christensen**, born 17 June 1879 in Skrøbelev, before his parents' marriage. Search Skrøbelev baptism, 1880/1890 censuses and the lægdsrulle to trace residence and later life.
- **Christian Jørgen Christensen**, born 1 December 1887 in Copenhagen, confirmed in Humble in 1902; absent from Danish censuses after 1901 and possibly an emigrant. Search the 1901 and 1911 censuses and Copenhagen Police emigration protocols 1902–1920 by name and birth parish.

The extension says Valdemar Emil Christensen took over Langø and was father of Lisbeth Skov, author of “En Langø-piges erindringer”. The memoir is a family-held private print. Scan it and preserve provenance; consider depositing a copy with Langelands Museum or the local archive with the family's permission.

claims.title: Ove Samuel Gedde: fødselsdato, mulig navnebror og moderens identitet
claims.claim: Ove Samuel Geddes identitet rummer flere uløste konflikter: 1778 mod 1788, 28. februar mod 28. maj, og to forskellige Fischer-søstre som mulig mor/stedmor. En hypotese foreslår to mænd med navnet Ove Samuel, men den er ikke bevist.
claims.evidence: Harbou angiver 28. februar 1778; en officerbiografi angiver 28. maj 1778; Anker angiver 28. maj 1788. Dossieret beskriver desuden en konflikt mellem den kanoniske moder Øllegaard Sophie Fischer og den foreslåede biologiske mor Frederikke Christiane Fischer.
claims.missing: Originale dåbs- og begravelsesindførsler i Fredensborg/Hof- og Slotsmenigheden og Fredrikstad samt vielses-/dødsindførsler, der kan skelne mulige navnebrødre og de to Fischer-søstre.
claims.next: Undersøg først dåb og tidlig død for en mulig Ove født 1778; kontrollér derefter Fredrikstad-dåben 1788 og Helsingør-begravelsen 1843, før person eller forældretilknytning ændres.

research_notes.title: Birth date
research_notes.context: 5. Ove Samuel Gedde — birth date and maternal identity
research_notes.text:
There is a real date conflict:
- Harbou (1897) gives 28 February 1778–10 March 1843.
- The current tree uses 28 February 1778.
- P.I. Liebe / E. Borgstrøm's officer biography (based on Rigsarkiv military notes) gives 28 May 1778–10 March 1843.
- Carl Johan Anker (1885) gives 28 May 1788; the OCR is marked unproofread and may conflate Ove with his father Hans Christopher.

The year 1778 has stronger support than 1788, but the exact day/month remains unresolved. Inspect the original baptism register in the relevant Fredensborg/Hof- og Slotsmenighed records and compare adjacent entries. Do not silently choose between 28 February and 28 May.

research_notes.title: Fischer sisters and mother conflict
research_notes.context: 5. Ove Samuel Gedde — birth date and maternal identity
research_notes.text:
The 2025 expanded research export corrected the proposed parentage: it links Ove (1778) to Hans Christopher Gedde and his first wife **Frederikke Christiane Fischer** (baptised 4 November 1745 at Toten, died 28 February 1787), while **Øllegaard Sophie Fischer** (born 5 August 1752 at Ullensaker, died 9 December 1821) is treated as his stepmother, married to Hans Christopher on 15 December 1789. DBL's Hans Christopher entry distinguishes these as two sisters.

However, the canonical `data/family.json` still links Ove to `p433`, Øllegaard Sophie Fischer, as mother. The expanded research export and canonical tree therefore disagree. This is a priority data-reconciliation issue, but do not change canonical parentage until the original baptism and marriage/death records have been checked.

Sources:
- [DBL, Hans Christopher Gedde](https://biografiskleksikon.lex.dk/Hans_Christopher_Gedde)
- [Harbou, Slægten von Kleist i Danmark](https://www.v-kleist.com/FG_allg/Kleist_in_Daenmark.pdf)
- [Anker, Biografiske Efterretninger om norske Officerer](https://arkivkopia.se/bok/runeberg-acj330bio)

research_notes.title: Ove Samuel I / II hypothesis
research_notes.context: 15. Gedde officer-line evidence conflicts and noble collateral ancestry
research_notes.text:
The segment 12 extension argues for two men:
- Ove Samuel I, born 28 February 1778, who died young;
- Ove Samuel II, born 28 May 1788 in Fredrikstad, died 10 March 1843 in Helsingør and buried 16 March at Skt. Mariæ.

It argues that Harbou attached the 1778 birth to the man who married in 1806 and died in 1843. This is a plausible conflation hypothesis, but the 1778 infant's death and the 1788 Fredrikstad baptism have not been inspected. Keep one existing p216 record with the competing dates and maternal possibilities documented; do not create a second Ove or move the canonical FAMC until the Fredensborg/Fredrikstad baptism and burial records are read.

claims.title: Christian Gedde/Giedde: to mulige identiteter i Ove Samuel-linjen
claims.claim: Kilderne beskriver to uforenelige kandidater til faderen til Samuel Christoph Gedde: Christian Gedde (1648–1707), kommandant på Møn, og Christian Giedde (født 1639, død 1705), knyttet til Kville. De må ikke flettes sammen alene på grund af navnelighed.

claims.missing: Samtidig dokumentation fra Kville og Møn, original vielse/familieoplysninger samt en kildekritisk gennemgang af Harbou, DBL og Schøllers officersgenealogi.
claims.next: Sammenlign de originale eller nær-samtidige kilder til begge mænd og fastslå, om der er tale om to personer eller en senere sammenblanding.

claims.title: Vibygård: skifte fra 1820 og to mulige Hans Jensen-husstande
claims.claim: Et skifte fra 1820 omtaler Maren Poulsdatter, hustru til en Hans Jensen, gartner ved Vibygård, og fire voksne børn. Det er ikke fastslået, at denne Hans Jensen er samme person som den kanoniske Hans Jensen (a66), der i 1822 blev gift med Margrethe Pedersdatter.
claims.evidence: Dossieret skelner udtrykkeligt mellem 1820-skiftet og Hans Jensen (a66), som folketællingen 1834 beskriver som aftægtsmand og tidligere gartner ved Wiibygaard.
claims.missing: Originalt skifte med afdødes identitet, hustru, børnenes navne, alder, bopæl og eventuelle værger; sammenhold med vielsen 1822 og folketællingen 1834.
claims.next: Find og læs originalskiftet fra 1820. Hold de to husstande adskilt, medmindre dokumentet giver en entydig identifikation.

research_notes.title: Canonical ancestor: Hans Jensen (`a66`)
research_notes.context: 3. Syv / Vibygård lead — keep two Hans Jensen households separate
research_notes.text: The current tree identifies Hans Jensen, former gardener at Vibygård, married Margrethe Pedersdatter in Syv in 1822. Their daughter Johanne Sophie Hansen was born in Syv in 1825. The 1834 census says Hans was a retired gardener at “Wiibygaard” and living on aftægt in Syv; he died in 1837. This explains why Johanne Sophie is sometimes recorded as born at Viby.

research_notes.title: Separate 1820 probate lead
research_notes.context: 3. Syv / Vibygård lead — keep two Hans Jensen households separate
research_notes.text: A separate probate extract reportedly names **Maren Poulsdatter**, wife of Hans Jensen, gardener at Vibygård, and four adult children (Poul, Jens, Peder and Ane). This is not automatically the same Hans Jensen as `a66`, whose wife in the current tree is Margrethe Pedersdatter and whose marriage is in 1822. Keep the households separate until the original probate identifies the gardener, spouse, children and dates.

research_notes.context: 10. Additional source targets recovered from the research extensions
research_notes.text: Karen Jensen (`p23`) is recorded as born 29 August 1852 by the Skarrild baptism and the 1875 Grindsted marriage, while the 1901 census gives 29 July. Prefer the baptism/marriage evidence and preserve the 1901 census discrepancy in the event notes rather than silently normalising it.

claims.title: Nordenbro-skiftet 1787: Christian Hansen og to ægteskaber
claims.claim: Et skifte fra 1787 i Nordenbro efter en Christian Hansen omtaler angiveligt to ægteskaber og flere børn. Det er ikke dokumenteret, at den afdøde er identisk med Christian Hansen (p114), født omkring 1806; skiftets børn kan muligvis tilhøre en senere generation.
claims.evidence: Dossieret beskriver skiftet som et endnu ikke tilknyttet spor og advarer specifikt mod at koble det til p114 alene på grund af navn og lokalitet.

research_notes.title: Family-held Sydlangeland death list
research_notes.context: 15. South Langeland source preservation and the 1787 probate
research_notes.text: “Dødsliste for Sydlangeland 1900–1970” is a printed register held in the family's copy and cited repeatedly in the tree. It carries names, occupations, residences, ages and death dates, including entries otherwise difficult to find in indexed church books. Scan it at high resolution, preserve its title/creator/publication details and keep the original; the family notes suggest depositing a copy with Langelands Museum/local archive if the family agrees.

research_notes.title: 1787 Nordenbro probate — Christian Hansen
research_notes.context: 15. South Langeland source preservation and the 1787 probate
research_notes.text: An open lead says a 1787 Nordenbro probate after **Christian Hansen** describes two marriages and several children in a local family. The extension suggests using it to test the identity of Christian Hansen (`p114`), born about 1806, who married Marie Madsdatter in 1829. The probate may concern a different Christian Hansen; the identity match is not established. Locate the correct probate jurisdiction and inspect the original for the deceased's age, spouse(s), children, residence and estate. Do not attach the family group to `p114` based only on the name and locality.

research_notes.title: Other open Langeland checks
research_notes.context: 15. South Langeland source preservation and the 1787 probate
research_notes.text:
- Verify the 1850 marriage of Jørgen Christensen (`p126`) and Bodil Margrethe Clausdatter (`p127`) in Skrøbelev/Magleby; their parents and nine children should be traced from the original records.
- Inspect Fangel parish records for Anne Katrine Jensdatter (`p113`).
- Inspect Snøde baptism records for Hans Berendsen (`p116`) and Anne Marie Olsdatter (`p117`).
- Inspect Magleby/Humble records 1780–1800 for Claus Madsen (`a254`), Ane Mortensdatter (`a255`), Mads Hansen (`a508`) and Karen Clausdatter (`a509`).
- Hennetved parish registers 1720–1800 are unindexed and are the route to the older Jørgensen branch (`a504`, `a505`, `a1008`–`a1011`).

research_notes.title: 16. Additional identity caution for the 1787 Nordenbro probate
research_notes.context: 16. Additional identity caution for the 1787 Nordenbro probate
research_notes.text: The 1787 probate lead is explicitly described in the original extension as **not yet connected to the tree**. It concerns a deceased Christian Hansen in Nordenbro with two marriages and several children; one possible son of the right generation could be the Christian Hansen (`p114`) who married Marie Madsdatter in 1829. The 42-year gap is too long for the deceased Christian to be p114's father; the probate's children might be p114's generation or siblings. Read the probate for a son Christian born around 1806, the two wives' names and the guardian list. If no matching Christian appears, record the negative and close the lead. Source cited in the old extension: Magleby-Nordenbro gods probate series; a web lead was elgezira.dk/historie.html.

claims.claim: Lovisa (Louise) Larsson (p17) er allerede en direkte ane og er født i Malmö 28. juni 1862. Hendes dødsindførsel nævner Niels Larsen (p34) som svensk far, men moderen mangler i det nuværende stamtræ.

research_notes.title: 6. Jørgensen / Malmö line
research_notes.context: 6. Jørgensen / Malmö line
research_notes.text:
Lovisa (Louise) Larsson (`p17`) is already a canonical ancestor of Evald through Aage Evald Oskar Jørgensen. She was born in Malmö on 28 June 1862 and died in Slagelse on 12 October 1910. Her death entry names Niels Larsen (`p34`) as her Swedish father; no mother is recorded in the current tree. The original potential-lead search for Lovisa should therefore be treated as partly resolved, not as an unconnected new person. Further work should inspect Malmö birth and household records to identify her mother and confirm the birth entry.

Niels Jørgensen (`p32`) married Johanne Sophie Hansdatter (`p33`) in Vor Frue, Copenhagen, on 7 July 1854. His birthplace is transcribed as “Hove/Høje sogn, Svendborg amt”; the parish is not identified. Preserve both readings until the original marriage entry is re-examined.

claims.title: Wilhelm Kroghs familie: forældre, bedsteforældre og søskende
claims.claim: En sekundær slægtsdatabase fra Lokalhistorisk Arkiv Ulkebøl forbinder Wilhelm/Vilhelm Krogh (født 9. oktober 1908 i Tastrup/Torstrup ved Flensborg) med forældrene Detlef Krogh (1876–1949) og Kirstine Marie Jensen (1878–1945), samt en søskendeflok på fem. Det kan åbne en dokumenterbar Krogh-side af Lorenz' juridiske faderskabssag, men forbindelsen er endnu ikke bekræftet i originale tyske eller danske registre.
claims.evidence: Ulkebøl-registreringen angiver forældrene, søskende og flere livsdatoer. En anden side for Bothille Marie Hansen og en side for Peter Krogh gentager dele af samme familiegruppe. Dossieret har også et lokalt Nybøl-holdingspor for en ældre Detlef Krogh, men dette beviser ikke i sig selv slægtskabet.

research_notes.title: Wilhelm Krogh's origins and family
research_notes.context: 12. Additional recovered leads: German-period Sønderjylland, Nybøl and Gedde collateral
research_notes.text:
The extension gives a reported birth for Wilhelm Krogh (`p12`) of 9 October 1908 at a place read as either **Tastrup** or **Vastrup**, Kreis Flensburg. The place name must remain ambiguous until the 11 July 1932 Egernsund marginal note is reread at high magnification. Search the 1908 birth register at Kreisarchiv Schleswig-Flensburg, after identifying the correct Standesamt jurisdiction.

A possible brother is Detlef Krogh, born 8 May 1905, who reportedly married in Broager in 1929 and had daughters registered in Nybøl in 1936 and 1940. The extension also notes a Detlef Krogh (born 1849) and Botilde (born 1850) in the 1921 Nybøl census as possible older relatives. These are **family-identification leads**, not established sibling or grandparent links. The best next step is the 1905 Detlef's 1929 Broager marriage entry, which should name his father; compare it with Wilhelm's 1908 German birth entry.

For Sønderjylland after 1867, use German Standesamt civil registers and Kreisarchiv holdings as well as the relevant church books. The old extension identifies Broagerlands Lokalarkiv's teglværk personnel protocols as another possible source for Egernsund workers.

research_notes.title: Older Lorenz namesake warning
research_notes.context: 12. Additional recovered leads: German-period Sønderjylland, Nybøl and Gedde collateral
research_notes.text: The research extension also distinguishes an earlier Lorenz Heinrich Frederiksen (`p24`) in the Broager line from another namesake (`pf12`) in Egernsund, and from this grandparent (`p6`, born 1932). Keep these people separate by birth date, parents, spouse and parish. Do not merge on the shared forenames.

research_notes.title: Wilhelm Krogh: separate 1908 namesake candidate
research_notes.context: 16. Broager / Nybøl / Rinkenæs collateral records and name traps
research_notes.text: The evidence audit notes a possible **Carl Vilhelm Krogh**, reportedly born 9 November 1908 in Tastrup/Flensburg and recorded in a 1925 Tandslet census, while this project's Wilhelm Krogh (`p12`) is recorded as born 9 October 1908 in Tastrup or Vastrup. Different given names and a one-month date difference mean they must not be merged. Request the 1908 Adelby church-book volume (book 2.3) from the Kirchenbuchamt Schleswig-Flensburg and compare exact parents and date with the Egernsund marginal note. The earlier candidate Detlef Krogh (born 1905) and the reported 1929 Broager marriage remain another route to the family.

claims.title: Paakjær i Nybøl: ejendomshistorie og Petersen-slægten
claims.claim: Paakjær er et centralt stedspor i familiens beretning om Sophus Petersen og den mulige biologiske faderskabslinje. Dossieret angiver, at Mathias Petersen opførte gården i 1879, og at den senere blev kaldt Sofus minde. Ejendommens historie kan kontrollere familiens sted- og husholdningsoplysninger, men kan ikke alene bevise biologisk faderskab.
claims.evidence: Familiedokumenter og den håndskrevne anetavle forbinder Mathias Petersen med opførelsen af Paakjær i 1879 og Peter Petersen/Sophus med gården. Nybøl 1921-folketællingsscanningen og Sophus' dåbs-/gravstensmateriale er bevaret i projektets kildemateriale. Dossieret peger desuden på *Fra Nybøl sogn* nr. 3 som lokalhistorisk ejendomskilde.
claims.missing: Den originale matrikel-/realregisterkæde, skøde eller fæste, brandforsikringsprotokol og eventuel byggesag, der kan identificere gårdens ejere og byggeår. Den lokale trykte oplysning skal kontrolleres mod selve ejendomsakterne.
claims.next: Find Paakjærs matrikelnummer og realregisterblad i Nybøl; følg derefter skøder og brandforsikringsprotokoller fra ca. 1879 til Peter Petersen og Sophus. Brug kirkebøger til personidentifikation og ejendomsakter kun til sted-/ejerhistorien.

research_notes.title: Paakjær farm records and the Sophus line
research_notes.context: 12. Additional recovered leads: German-period Sønderjylland, Nybøl and Gedde collateral
research_notes.text:
Mathias Petersen (`sofus_ff`) reportedly built Paakjær in Nybøl in 1879; the farm was later called “Sofus minde”. This gives a collateral archival route: building application, fire-insurance policy and property records may identify the builder, owners and estate history. These records can corroborate household/property context but do not prove Lorenz's paternity.

The Nybøl 1921 census scan and Sophus's 1903 baptism/grave scan are preserved in `leads/` and linked above. For the possible half-sibling group, the current citations cover Nybøl girls born 1938, 1940 and 1943. Read the register beyond 1943 before assuming a fourth daughter; if the Norway lead is correct, search Norwegian marriage banns and newspaper notices after identifying her full name.

claims.title: Gedde-familiens udvandring: Olaf til Shanghai og Emil til Argentina
claims.claim: To collateralspor i Gedde-familien peger på oversøisk udvandring: Olaf Gedde har et registreret udvandringskontraktnummer 3534 fra 11. juli 1904 via agent Haugsted med Shanghai som destination; Emil Gedde forbindes med Eldorado-kolonien i Argentina gennem fotografihenvisningerne B9886 og B9790. De to personer og deres videre livsforløb skal dokumenteres hver for sig.

Rigsarkivets vejledning bekræfter, at politiets udvandringskontrakter 1868–1959 kan indeholde navn, alder, stilling, bopæl, fødested, bestemmelsessted og kontraktdato; arkivserierne omfatter direkte og indirekte udvandrerregistre.
claims.missing: Olafs originale kontrakt/genpart, skib og ankomst i Shanghai samt senere bopæl/død; Emils fulde udvandringsidentitet, ankomst til Argentina, ophold i Eldorado og eventuelle efterkommere. Fotografierne B9886/B9790 skal ses og billedteksterne aflæses.
claims.next: Slå Olaf op i Københavns Politis udvandrerprotokol omkring kontraktnr. 3534 og 11. juli 1904; følg skibsekspedition og Shanghai-kilder. For Emil: identificér fuldt navn/fødselsdata fra billedkatalog B9886/B9790 og søg derefter i argentinske koloniregistre og dansk-argentinske kirkebøger.

research_notes.title: Claus Gaardsted (`p72`) and Karen Christensdatter
research_notes.context: 2. Gaardsted / Vosnæsgaard / Rolsøgård
research_notes.text:
**Status: strong sibling clue; parentage unresolved.**

The Rolsøgård G302 alphabetical probate index, under Niels Jensen Degn in Vrinners, probate no. 11, 14 May 1787, folio 39, records:

> “Arv i boet til afdødes stedbørn efter Christen Christensen Tohde? foged i Dejret (skifte 1764) til datter Karen Christensdatter LV: broder Claus Gaardsted forpagter på Vosnæsgård.”

The index identifies Karen Christensdatter as sister of Claus Gaardsted, tenant at Vosnæsgaard, and says he acted as her lavværge (legal guardian). It points to an earlier 1764 probate for bailiff Christen Christensen “Tohde?” in Dejret.

**Do not infer** that Tohde was Claus's or Karen's biological father. The wording refers to stepchildren and is not sufficiently clear to establish biological parentage. The original 1764 probate must be located and read. Also inspect the original 1787 folio 39 rather than relying solely on the alphabetical index.

Source: [Rolsøgård G302 index, 1778–1816](https://slaegt.dk/media/jnnnvuml/alfabetisk-navneliste-og-skifteuddrag-til-rols%C3%B8g%C3%A5rd-gods-g302-mols-herred-1778-1816-1818.pdf).

The older Jørgensen frontier notes identify two children of Niels Jørgensen (`p32`) and Johanne Sophie Hansen (`p33`) who survived infancy:

This is collateral research, not a missing direct-ancestor link.

claims.title: Sophus Petersen: mulig fjerde datter og halvsøskende

research_notes.title: 3. Sophus Petersen's reported daughters / possible half-siblings
research_notes.context: 3. Sophus Petersen's reported daughters / possible half-siblings
research_notes.text:
The family account says Sophus and wife Christine had four daughters and that one moved to Norway. The current tree note elsewhere names only three daughters (Gerda and two others), while the family document says “4 døtre”. This is a count discrepancy. Nybøl church-book searches are reported for girls born 1938, 1940 and 1943; a fourth daughter has not been located. Recheck the full family group and a wider date range. Do not assume a fourth daughter solely from the count without recording the source for it.

If the relationship to Sophus is supported, the daughters would be possible maternal/paternal half-siblings depending on the exact parentage, but this is downstream of the paternity question and should not be used as proof of it.

claims.title: Rasmus Jensen og Anne Christine Hansens vielse i Dybbøl 1866
claims.claim: Vielsen 18. september 1866 i Dybbøl er et centralt kontrolpunkt for Rasmus Jensen og Anne Christine Hansen i Else Geddes slægtslinje. Arkivkatalogerne bekræfter, hvor vielsesbogen findes, men selve indførslen er endnu ikke læst i originalen.
claims.evidence: Dossieret henviser til Dybbøl Ab 4 (1861–1927), der omfatter vielser 1861–1906, og Rigsarkivets indeks over Dybbøl-vielser 1723–1900. Vieweradgang gav hidtil kun en skal.
claims.missing: Original vielsesindførsel med alder, bopæl, fædre, forlovere og præcis navneform; særligt forældrene til Rasmus skal kontrolleres.

research_notes.title: 9. Dybbøl / Broager collateral line
research_notes.context: 9. Dybbøl / Broager collateral line
research_notes.text:
Jens Jensen (`p26`), father of Else Gedde Jensen, is recorded as son of Rasmus Jensen and Christine Hansen. He married Paula Gedde in 1907. Rasmus Jensen (`p52`) married Anne Christine Hansen (`p53`) in Dybbøl on 18 September 1866. The exact marriage entry remains to be visually inspected; prior Arkivalieronline access returned a viewer shell. The archival series description confirms that Dybbøl Ab 4 (1861–1927) contains marriages 1861–1906; a separate official Rigsarkivet index for Dybbøl marriages 1723–1900 is also catalogued, but its image viewer currently exposes only a shell to this research pass. These catalogue descriptions confirm where to look, not the contents of the 1866 entry. Transcribe witnesses, ages, residences and fathers from the original page before treating the proposed parents Hans Hansen and Ellen Kock as independently verified.

**Catalogue confirmation (16 November 2026):** Rigsarkivet's [Dybbøl register index](https://arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk/da/other/index-creator/29/725983/18484622) lists a marriage index for 1723–1900. The printed archival inventory confirms that [Dybbøl Ab 4](https://slaegtsbibliotek.dk/2024/941454.pdf) covers marriages 1861–1906. Neither catalogue/index description has yet yielded a readable transcription of the 18 September 1866 entry. See also [Rigsarkivet's church-book guide](https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/vejledning/kirkeboeger-borgerlige-vielser-m-m/kirkeboeger-kom-godt-i-gang/).

claims.title: von Kleist: middelalderlig Muttrin-linje og kildekonflikter

claims.evidence: Gennemgangen skelner mellem dokumenter fra 1248–1477, Muttrin-forbindelserne fra 1364 og frem, 1555–1618-slægtsoptegnelser og senere Reimer/Bartes-rekonstruktioner. Dossieret registrerer væsentlige modsigelser og moderne kildekritik.
